journal_articles.title: GATA transcription factors coordinate developmental progression in the arabidopsis root.
journal_articles.abstract: Proper organ development requires the coordination of cell type-specific differentiation programs with general maturation processes through precise spatiotemporal gene regulation. In plants, where RNA polymerase pausing is not well established, alternative mechanisms must ensure this coordination. Here, using single-cell resolution transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility data, we reconstruct developmental trajectories of the Arabidopsis root ground tissue to investigate these mechanisms. We describe phased transcriptional landscapes governing the transition from stem cell to early differentiation, in which chromatin accessibility marks the activation of key developmental regulators. A major transcriptional switch in the late meristematic zone, underpinned by extensive chromatin remodeling, drives the transition from cell division to differentiation. Leveraging machine learning to examine integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility trajectories, we identify GATA transcription factors (TFs) as central coordinators of this switch; a role we validate experimentally. We show that the GATA TFs sit at the tipping point of a feedback-driven bistable system that integrates inputs from auxin and cytokinin to balance proliferation and differentiation, ensuring temporal precision in root development at both the tissue and organ scales.

journal_articles.title: Hoxa10 governs lifelong skeletal stem cell maintenance and bone repair.
journal_articles.abstract: Skeletal stem and progenitor cells (SSPCs) sustain bone homeostasis and regeneration throughout life, yet the transcriptional programs that preserve their identity remain poorly defined. Here we identify the distal Hox gene Hoxa10 as a cell-autonomous regulator of skeletal stem cell maintenance. Using inducible genetic deletion, lineage tracing, single-cell transcriptomics, and injury models, we show that loss of Hoxa10 leads to progressive depletion of SSPCs, impaired bone regeneration, and defective matrix organization. Mechanistically, Hoxa10 maintains the undifferentiated state of skeletal stem cells by restraining premature osteogenic, adipogenic, and chondrogenic commitment, while promoting collagen III production and collagen fiber alignment within regenerative niches. Hoxa10-dependent regulation of extracellular matrix composition is restricted to primitive progenitors and is uncoupled from osteoblast differentiation. Notably, transient depletion of distal Hox genes in primary human SSPCs recapitulates the murine defects in proliferation, self-renewal, and differentiation restraint. Together, these findings define a conserved Hox-dependent program that preserves skeletal stem cell identity and regenerative competence, revealing how developmental transcription factors are repurposed to sustain the adult skeleton across the life span.

journal_articles.title: Male fertility is independent of Enh13 control of Sox9 testicular expression.
journal_articles.abstract: Testis development requires precise temporal control of Sox9 expression, which is rapidly activated to initiate testis development and maintained to preserve Sertoli cell identity and male fertility. The distal enhancer, Enh13, is essential for Sox9 upregulation as its constitutive deletion causes complete XY male-to-female sex reversal. Whether Enh13 is required across distinct developmental stages remains unexplored. We show that early gonadal deletion of Enh13 fully recapitulates XY sex reversal, demonstrating that Enh13 is strictly required to initiate the male pathway. In contrast, Sertoli cell-specific deletion of Enh13 after sex determination has no effect on Sox9 expression, testis architecture, or male fertility, revealing that Enh13 is dispensable for Sox9 maintenance in differentiated testis. Chromatin accessibility identifies candidate enhancers gaining activity after sex determination, suggesting a potential regulatory handoff within the Sox9 locus. Finally, duplicating Enh13 in the endogenous mouse locus fails to recapitulate human XX sex reversal, suggesting that it may not be solely Enh13 sequence duplication that led to this phenotype. This work represents an in vivo demonstration of enhancer handoff during development, enabling temporally controlled interrogation of regulatory logic.

journal_articles.title: Genetic dissection of cell type-specific congenital heart disease variants reveals ETS1 control of vascular smooth muscle cell fate.
journal_articles.abstract: Numerous congenital heart disease (CHD) risk variants lie in cis-regulatory elements, yet the impact of variants in repressed and bivalent chromatin on cell type-specific heart development is unclear. Here, we generated a single-cell multiomic atlas of human cardiac differentiation by jointly profiling H3K27ac, H3K27me3, H3K4me3, and transcriptomes in individual cells, classifying cis-regulatory elements into six chromatin states, enabling prioritization of 610 CHD-associated noncoding variants enriched in lineage- and state-specific regulatory elements, including repressive and bivalent regions. CRISPR knockin of selected variants perturbed nearby gene expression and impaired cardiac differentiation. Dissection of a Polycomb-marked variant near ETS1 (ETS proto-oncogene 1) revealed local H3K27me3 loss, H3K27ac gain, and ETS1 up-regulation, which redirects differentiation toward second-heart-field progenitors with epithelial characteristics at early stages and, ultimately, highly migratory ETS1+ vascular smooth muscle cells. Together, our work establishes a single-cell chromatin-state framework for interpreting noncoding CHD risk variants and uncovers an ETS1-driven program linking Polycomb-deregulated noncoding variation to aberrant vascular smooth muscle fate commitment during human cardiogenesis.

journal_articles.title: Plagl2 reprograms adult mouse retinal Müller glia for proliferation and injury-enhanced neurogenic competence.
journal_articles.abstract: Müller glia (MG) in the adult mammalian retina have long been recognized as a potential endogenous source for the regeneration of lost retinal neurons. However, existing MG reprogramming strategies yield an incomplete regenerative response by favoring either proliferation or neurogenic differentiation. Here, we show that the zinc-finger transcription factor gene Plagl2, previously shown to reactivate quiescent neural stem cells, is sufficient to reprogram adult mouse MG into a progenitor-like state with coupled proliferative and neurogenic competence. Using histology, time-lapse imaging, and single-cell transcriptomics, we find that Plagl2 drives regulated rounds of MG cell cycle re-entry, while N-methyl-D-aspartate-induced retinal injury further promotes the acquisition of neurogenic competence biased toward inner nuclear layer neuronal identities. These findings indicate that Plagl2 regulates mammalian MG reprogramming, and supports a broader approach to tissue regeneration through the adaptation of reprogramming modules across distinct cell types.

journal_articles.title: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity.
journal_articles.abstract: Glioblastoma is incurable and resistant to therapy despite genomic stability under treatment1-8, suggesting that non-genetic cellular plasticity is a central driver of progression. Whether such plasticity reflects stochastic state switching or is governed by predictable gene regulation has remained unclear9-13. Here we introduce scDORI (single-cell deep multi-omic regulatory inference)-a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene-regulatory networks at single-cell resolution-and apply it to single-nucleus multiome profiles of more than one million cells from primary glioblastomas. Integrating computational inference with systematic perturbation screens across patient-derived models, we show that a structured regulatory program with an asymmetric interplay of activators and repressors governs cellular plasticity in glioblastoma. The resulting transition landscape is hierarchical and predictable, but permits cross-lineage trajectories that are absent from normal neurodevelopment. Within this landscape, low-plasticity states such as the neuronal-like state are not stable differentiation end points but actively maintained configurations, stabilized by a network of safeguard repressors that silence alternative fates. We identify MYT1L as the dominant member of this network, and show that it binds to and represses master regulators of every alternative state to consolidate neuronal-like identity. MYT1L restricted plasticity even under standard-of-care therapy and suppressed tumour growth and invasion in vivo. Conversely, loss of MYT1L reactivated plasticity and accelerated malignant features, indicating that low-plasticity identity requires continuous repression. These findings reframe malignant cell state stability as a balance between activation and continuous repression, and nominate safeguard repressors as candidate therapeutic targets that are distinct from differentiation-inducing activators, with potential relevance across cancers in which phenotypic switching drives therapy resistance.

journal_articles.title: Coupling of cell proliferation to the segmentation clock promotes robust somite scaling.
journal_articles.abstract: How developing tissues coordinate growth and patterning to maintain their proportions remains unclear. During vertebrate somitogenesis, somite size scales with the presomitic mesoderm (PSM), where morphogen gradients and oscillating Notch, Wnt (wingless and Int-1), and fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signaling regulate segmentation. We find that proliferation is uniformly distributed throughout the oscillating PSM and, using long-term single-cell tracking and microfluidic entrainment in mouse embryo tails, provide evidence for functional coupling between cell-cycle progression and the segmentation clock, likely involving periodic cyclin D1 regulation among other mechanisms. A minimal model suggests that this coupling promotes uniform PSM growth and morphogen dilution, supporting robust somite formation. Loss of clock function increases Mesp2 patterning irregularity, whereas inhibiting proliferation alters morphogen profiles and somite scaling. Human in vitro somitogenesis models show a comparable clock-cell-cycle phase relationship, suggesting conservation across species. Together, these findings link clock-coupled proliferation to coordinated tissue growth, robust patterning, and scaling.

journal_articles.title: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory underlies glioblastoma heterogeneity.
journal_articles.abstract: Cancer cells show highly heterogeneous and plastic states in glioblastoma, an incurable brain tumour1-5. However, how these malignant states arise and whether they follow defined cellular trajectories across tumours is poorly understood. Here we generated a deep single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma that pairs transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling of 12 tumours across many regions. We identify that glioblastoma heterogeneity is driven by spatially patterned transitions of cancer cells from developmental-like states towards those defined by a glial injury response and hypoxia. This cellular trajectory regionalizes tumours into distinct tissue microenvironments and manifests in a molecularly conserved manner across tumours as well as genetically distinct tumour subclones. Consistently, using a new deep-learning framework to map cancer cell states jointly with clones in situ, we show that tumour subclones are finely spatially intermixed through glioblastoma tissue microenvironments. We validate this cellular trajectory by using somatic mutation-based hierarchies in vivo and an experimental patient-derived organoid model ex vivo. Finally, we show that this cancer cell trajectory is intimately linked to myeloid heterogeneity and unfolds across regionalized myeloid signalling environments. Our findings define a stereotyped trajectory of cancer cells in glioblastoma and unify glioblastoma tumour heterogeneity into a tractable cellular and tissue framework.

journal_articles.title: Reconstructing the emergence of the human chorion via Hippo-mediated trophoblast induction.
journal_articles.abstract: Differential Hippo-LATS-YAP signalling controls the first mammalian cell-fate decision, yet how human trophectoderm specification progresses to chorion formation remains unknown. Here we establish a developmentally informed model in which LATS kinase inhibition initiates the trophectoderm trajectory without exogenous morphogens. Stage matching to an integrated embryo-chorion single-cell reference revealed ordered progression from early trophectoderm to secondary chorionic lineages. Whole-genome bisulfite sequencing showed a naive-like hypomethylated state followed by remethylation, with key known placenta-associated imprinted domains retaining methylation and allelic bias. We then established a three-dimensional human chorion model by agitating induced-cell aggregates in suspension, yielding secondary chorionic lineages that self-organized with outward-facing trophoblast polarity and inside-out stromal-epithelial topology. Endogenous WNT signalling was dispensable for initial trophectoderm induction but regulated later chorionic lineage balance. Isolating CLDN6+ITGA6- cells identified a proEVT-like intermediate with villous and extravillous potential. Together, this framework connects human trophectoderm induction to three-dimensional chorion modelling and enables investigation of placental specification.

journal_articles.title: A SAGA-like AP2-P-ARP1-GCN5 transcriptional complex targets pathogenesis-associated genes during the blood-stage development of Babesia gibsoni.
journal_articles.abstract: Babesiosis is an increasingly recognized tick-borne zoonosis. The asexual blood stage of its causative agent, Babesia, drives pathological damages in the host and can cause severe or fatal human infections. Nevertheless, the transcriptional regulatory mechanisms that control this developmental stage remain poorly characterized. Here, we identified a novel ApiAP2 transcription factor (AP2-P; pathogenesis), which is essential in the blood-stage development of B. gibsoni. Nuclear import of AP2-P is inhibited by ivermectin, which is likely mediated via the IMPα/β pathway. Importantly, AP2-P forms a SAGA-like complex with the histone acetyltransferase GCN5 and a novel AP2-P related protein 1 (ARP1). Conditional knockdown of ARP1 or GCN5 results in reduced parasite growth rates accompanied by alterations in expression profiles and chromatin accessibility of pathogenesis-related genes. ChIP-seq data indicate that the complex associates with both euchromatic regions marked by H3K9ac and heterochromatic regions marked by H3K9me3, and it also targets many pathogenic genes by recognizing specific DNA motif, including those involved in invasion, antigenic variation, drug resistance, and sexual-stage development. Notably, normal genomic distribution pattern of AP2-P likewise depends on ARP1 or GCN5. Collectively, our study suggests a SAGA-like epigenetic module responsible for pathogenesis of Babesia gibsoni during asexual blood stage.

journal_articles.title: A family of small proteins links c-di-GMP riboswitch signaling with sporulation in Clostridioides difficile.
journal_articles.abstract: Cyclic diguanosine monophosphate (c-di-GMP) is a second messenger that coordinates lifestyle transitions, virulence, and developmental processes in bacteria. In Clostridioides difficile, elevated c-di-GMP levels inhibit sporulation, but the underlying mechanism remained unclear. Here, we identified a conserved family of small, membrane-associated proteins encoded by c-di-GMP riboswitch-regulated genes. Transcriptomic analyses revealed that c-di-GMP represses these genes, and reporter assays demonstrated riboswitch-dependent transcriptional regulation via premature termination mechanism. Overexpression of a single gene, CD1980.2, was sufficient to trigger the transcriptional activation of sporulation genes, including sigma factors and their regulons, and to increase spore formation. Conversely, sporulation efficiency decreased proportionally with the number of deleted small-protein genes, and the strain lacking all seven genes displayed a severe sporulation defect, underscoring their cumulative and functionally redundant roles. Elevating c-di-GMP levels in the deletion mutant did not further reduce sporulation, supporting a model in which c-di-GMP inhibits spore formation by repressing the expression of this small-protein family. Thus, our work establishes these small proteins, encoded by c-di-GMP riboswitch-regulated genes, as important regulators of spore formation in C. difficile, a process essential for pathogen persistence and transmission.

journal_articles.title: RhoA Y42C drives cell plasticity and PD-1-mediated immune evasion of diffuse gastric cancer.
journal_articles.abstract: Diffuse gastric cancer (DGC) is an aggressive gastric cancer subtype with a poor prognosis. The RHOA Y42C mutation is recurrent in DGC, but its independent oncogenic role is unclear. Next-Generation Sequencing of 431 DGC cases revealed that most RHOA mutations occurred without CDH1 alterations. Using genetically engineered gastric organoids, we show that RhoaY42C, along with KrasG12D and Trp53 loss (RKP), induces DGC, independently of Cdh1 loss. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal that RKP tumors exhibit mucinous histopathology and a specific lineage trajectory from Aqp5+ cells to Muc1/Muc4+ cells. RKP tumors create an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment where AREG, transactivated by RhoA Y42C-YAP1, causes T cell exhaustion via PD-1 upregulation. Unlike E-cadherin loss-associated DGC, RKP tumors are highly susceptible to PD-1 blockade. Additionally, the RHOA Y42C mutation correlates with PD-1 upregulation in human DGC samples. These findings redefine the oncogenic role of RhoA Y42C, confirming its sufficiency for DGC development and suggesting PD-1 inhibition as a viable therapeutic option for DGC patients carrying this mutation.

journal_articles.title: A framework for genome-wide characterization of DNA methylation and variant effect prediction.
journal_articles.abstract: DNA methylation plays a critical role in many essential biological processes, including transcriptional regulation, genomic imprinting, chromosomal maintenance, genomic stability and development, and has phenotypic and disease impacts. However, genome-wide characterization of methylation patterns across cell types and tissues remains a major challenge. Here, to address this, we present a framework that enables systematic genome-wide analysis of methylation and sequence-based prediction of context-specific methylation effects of variants. Our data-driven discovery of methylation classes reveals context-dependent roles for methylation across tissues, cell types and regions of the genome. The framework also includes Wreath, a deep learning-based sequence model specifically designed to accurately predict the context-dependent impact of any genetic variant on methylation. These developments leverage a compendium that harmonizes disparate methylation profiles from disparate studies including over 90 tissues and cell types. Using Wreath, we systematically characterized the impact of noncoding pathogenic variants on tissue-specific methylation, generating mechanistic hypotheses for individual regulatory variants. We make the full framework, including the compendium, the methylation classes and the model, available for use by the community.

journal_articles.title: Human hair-bearing skin organoids reveal cell type-specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1.
journal_articles.abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. To model this complex environment, we used human hair-bearing skin organoids and combined single-cell spatial transcriptomics with imaging to map viral spread and host responses across skin architecture. Our data suggest delayed progression of the HSV-1 life cycle in epidermal keratinocytes and hair follicle cells compared to the dermis. Infection triggered spatially organized host responses, including induction of IER3 in papillary fibroblasts. In basal keratinocytes, IRF3 was up-regulated in both infected and neighboring uninfected cells, consistent with paracrine activation of antiviral signaling. Inflammatory responses were compartmentalized in a cell type-specific manner, with TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) induced in papillary fibroblasts and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) induced in keratinocytes. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays confirmed secretion of these cytokines and the TNF-α-responsive chemokines CXCL2 and CXCL10. CXCL2 expression was enriched in cells adjacent to TNF-α-expressing cells, highlighting spatial coordination of inflammatory signaling. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair-bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host-HSV-1 interactions.

journal_articles.title: A bivalent chromatin reader-WOX5 module maintains root stem cell niche in Arabidopsis.
journal_articles.abstract: Root stem cell niche maintenance requires precise control of quiescent center (QC) and columella stem cell (CSC) activity, yet how chromatin regulators interface with key transcription factors remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the bivalent chromatin reader EARLY BOLTING IN SHORT DAYS (EBS) as an essential regulator of root stem cell maintenance in Arabidopsis. A strong ebs-1 mutant shows CSC differentiation and QC activation, and EBS function requires its histone mark-recognizing BAH and PHD domains and a C-terminal SUMO-interacting motif. EBS physically interacts with the QC master regulator WUSCHEL-RELATED HOMEOBOX 5 (WOX5) and, together with WOX5, activates WOX5 transcription by promoting EBS enrichment at the WOX5 promoter. Consistently, wox5-1 is epistatic to ebs-1, and WOX5 overexpression rescues the ebs-1 stem cell defects. Together, this work uncovers a chromatin-based positive autoregulatory loop that integrates histone-state recognition and transcriptional feedback, providing a framework for epigenetic control of stem cell fate in plants.

journal_articles.title: A single-cell comprehensive atlas of leukemia and its microenvironment.
journal_articles.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains highly lethal, with treatment failure and relapse driven by dynamic cellular states and evolving interactions within the leukemic ecosystem. In this study, we built a comprehensive atlas of leukemia and its microenvironment (CALM) by integrating single-cell profiling from 73 AML samples and 9 healthy donors, bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) from 87 newly diagnosed patients, and 4 paired bone marrow and peripheral blood single-cell data. All datasets were linked to clinical, cytogenetic, molecular, and treatment-response annotations. Immune analysis revealed diverse T cell distribution across disease status, where patients with persistent disease exhibited greater clonal expansion. Machine learning modeling on conventional T cells identified a T-cell signature pertinent to AML and outcomes, which were validated in two cohorts. CALM is a publicly accessible and interactive portal (calm.mdanderson.org) for exploring cellular compartments, cell-cell interactions, and longitudinal transcriptional and clonal dynamics to enable hypothesis generation, biomarker discovery, and target validation.

journal_articles.title: Clearing perivascular light chain-derived amyloid to counteract aging-associated decline in liver regeneration.
journal_articles.abstract: Aging impairs organ regeneration, with insufficient angiogenesis as a key contributor. Here, we show that the endothelial immunoproteasome subunit PSMB8 is upregulated in aged mouse livers after partial hepatectomy. Endothelial PSMB8 deletion or PR-957 inhibition promotes angiogenesis and rescues liver regeneration. diGly proteomics identifies TAZ (transcriptional co-activator with PDZ-binding motif) as a ubiquitin-dependent immunoproteasome substrate, and TAZ activation restores aged liver regeneration. Aging triggers the infiltration of CD38+IGLC1+ IgM B cells and aberrant perivascular light chain-derived amyloid deposition in the liver. Recombinant light chain-derived amyloid fibrils directly induce PSMB8 expression in vitro. Anselamimab-mediated light chain-derived amyloid clearance mitigates immunoproteasome overactivation and restores regeneration. Single-cell RNA sequencing confirms that anselamimab reverses aging-induced endothelial marker loss and inflammatory gene upregulation. Our findings establish a pathway linking perivascular light chain-derived amyloid deposition to regenerative decline via endothelial immunoproteasome activation, suggesting amyloid clearance as a promising therapeutic strategy for aging-associated decline in liver regeneration.

journal_articles.title: Machine learning-assisted Repli-Histo labeling reveals distinct transcription-dependent constraints on chromatin motion in living cells.
journal_articles.abstract: Genomic DNA is wrapped around core histones to form nucleosomes, which are organized in cells from euchromatin to heterochromatin with distinct genome functions. Although transcription is known to shape chromatin behavior in live cells, it remains unclear how different transcription systems act across chromatin classes and nuclear subcompartments. We develop machine learning-assisted Repli-Histo labeling to classify euchromatin and heterochromatin classes (classes IA, IB, II, and III) and combine it with single-nucleosome imaging in living human cells. Nucleosome motion is progressively constrained from euchromatin to heterochromatin. RNA polymerase II inhibition by THZ1, DRB, or α-amanitin increases nucleosome motion in euchromatic classes IA and IB and in heterochromatin around nucleoli, but not at the nuclear periphery. In contrast, RNA polymerase I inhibition by CX-5461 selectively increases nucleosome motion in Class III heterochromatin around nucleoli. Our study reveals that Pol II and Pol I transcription shape chromatin behavior in distinct chromatin classes and nuclear subcompartments.

journal_articles.title: An ECM-driven mechanotransductive signaling module promotes NKX6.1-enriched human pancreatic progenitor formation.
journal_articles.abstract: Efficient generation of insulin-producing beta cells from human pluripotent stem cells requires precise specification of PDX1+/NKX6.1+ pancreatic progenitors, a developmental bottleneck that limits lineage fidelity and reproducibility across differentiation platforms. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized extracellular matrix (ECM)-coupled mechanotransductive module that promotes an NKX6.1-enriched pancreatic progenitor state. Transcriptomic profiling and targeted perturbations revealed that isoxazole-9 (ISX-9) engages a collagen-TRPV-Ca2+-Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) axis, linking ECM sensing to NKX6.1 regulation. Collagen I/IV supplementation and TRPV agonists phenocopied ISX-9, whereas inhibition of integrin α1/α2, TRPV channels, or CaMKII abrogated its effect. Downstream of CaMKII, relief of histone deacetylase 4 (HDAC4)-mediated myocyte enhancer factor 2 (MEF2) repression contributed to NKX6.1 regulation, while increased cycling of NKX6.1+ cells accompanied expansion of the progenitor pool. Temporally restricted activation of this module by ISX-9 increased PDX1+/NKX6.1+ progenitors and yielded stem cell-derived islets (SC-islets) with enhanced glucose responsiveness. These findings provide a basis for optimizing microenvironmental cues to improve the generation of NKX6.1-enriched pancreatic progenitors and functional SC-islets.

journal_articles.title: Venousization enables angiogenesis in the absence of VEGFR signalling.
journal_articles.abstract: The vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) ligand and its main receptor VEGFR2 are considered to be essential for endothelial differentiation, proliferation, sprouting and survival1. Blood vessels cannot form in growing embryos or tissues when VEGF-VEGFR2 signalling is compromised in all cells2,3. The anti-VEGF antibody, which can block angiogenesis in cancer, wound healing or ischaemic diseases, is among the most widely used antibodies in the clinic. However, vascular resistance to anti-VEGF therapy has been reported4,5. Here we used iFlpMosaics and iSuRe-HadCre to induce and track genetic mosaics of endothelial cells (ECs) lacking VEGFR2 during the entire embryonic and postnatal development. These Vegfr2-knockout (Vegfr2KO) ECs adapted, proliferated normally and competed with wild-type cells over time, eventually forming a substantial portion of the vascular network in most organs. Vegfr2KO ECs could not sprout during the first wave of angiogenesis in most tissues, because this process is highly VEGF-dependent and favours growth and mobilization of wild-type ECs. However, owing to their inability to respond to VEGF, Vegfr2KO ECs became dominant in veins, which represented a long-term and continuous source of ECs for subsequent waves of VEGF-independent angiogenesis. Comparative single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of ECs with acute and long-term loss of VEGFR2 identified both common and organ-specific molecular mechanisms of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss. These included significant endothelial venousization and upregulation of ligands for VEGFR1 and VEGFR3. VEGFR1 only partially compensated for VEGFR2 loss in capillary ECs, whereas VEGFR3 compensated only in arterial ECs. Loss of the three VEGF receptors did not compromise venous growth. Notably, loss of the master regulator of venous development, NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), significantly compromised expansion of Vegfr2KO ECs. This work has implications for our understanding of the role of VEGF receptors in angiogenesis and demonstrates venousization as a mechanism of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss during angiogenesis.

journal_articles.title: Estimating the completeness of large-scale single-cell sequencing projects.
journal_articles.abstract: During embryonic development, cells undergo differentiation into highly specialized cell types. Capitalizing on single-cell RNA sequencing, many initiatives and substantial resources are cataloguing these differentiated cell types by their transcriptomic profiles. Despite the extensive efforts to profile various organs and their cellular compositions, we lack metrics to assess the completeness of the sequencing projects. In this cellular biodiversity analysis, we leverage the increasingly available single-cell data together with statistical methods, originally developed for assessing the species richness of ecological communities, to estimate dataset completeness based on current data from single-cell profiling technologies. Deriving from such cellular richness estimates, we establish a practical statistical framework that enables reliable assessment of the completeness of any large-scale single-cell profiling project, after which additional sequencing efforts do not anymore reveal new cellular clusters. Such estimates can serve as stoppage-points for the ongoing sequencing projects, hence guiding a more cost-efficient completion of the profiling of various human tissues.

journal_articles.title: Joule-heated regenerable carbon dioxide capture filter for demand-controlled ventilation in indoor applications.
journal_articles.abstract: Carbon dioxide (CO2) plays a key role in indoor air quality and is traditionally managed through ventilation, which often increases energy consumption. This work proposes a demand-controlled ventilation system integrated with a CO2 filter to reduce both indoor CO2 levels and ventilation-related energy use. The modular CO2 capture filter was manufactured by spray-coating an amine-functionalized solid sorbent onto a carbon fiber substrate, enabling rapid thermal regeneration via Joule heating within 15 min at 100 °C. System-scale operation was optimized using Differential Evolution, and a deep neural network was employed as a surrogate model to rapidly approximate the optimized control parameters across varying indoor conditions. Simulation-based analysis indicates the proposed system could lower energy loads by about 14.9-25% compared to conventional systems, while maintaining indoor CO2 at 600 ppm under various outdoor conditions. This work establishes an implementation pathway spanning material characterization, lab-scale tests, and model-based system-level analysis.

last_author.name: Yong Tae Kang
last_author.affiliation: School of Mechanical Engineering, Korea University, Seoul, South Korea. ytkang@korea.ac.kr.

journal_articles.title: Reconstructing the single-cell spatiotemporal dynamics of glioblastoma invasion.
journal_articles.abstract: Glioblastoma invasion into healthy brain tissue remains a major barrier to effective treatment, but the dynamic single-cell behaviors underlying this process remain difficult to measure across patient models. Here, we introduce GlioTrace, an ex vivo imaging and computational framework for real-time tracking of glioblastoma invasion in patient-derived xenograft brain slices. Combining whole-specimen confocal microscopy with machine learning-based morphology classification and probabilistic modeling of state transitions, GlioTrace reconstructs how tumor cells switch between invasion phenotypes and how these dynamics are shaped by local tissue context and therapy. Across six patient-derived models, GlioTrace reveals that invasion plasticity is patient-specific, spatially organized, and modulated by vascular proximity and microglial interaction. Targeted therapies selectively alter phenotype composition and transition probabilities, whereas standard-of-care treatment enriches a highly motile, transition-connected branching state consistent with a treatment-tolerant invasive phenotype. Thus, GlioTrace makes glioblastoma invasion a measurable dynamic process for comparing patient-specific treatment responses in living brain tissue.

last_author.name: Sven Nelander
last_author.affiliation: Department of Immunology, Genetics and Pathology, Uppsala University, Uppsala, Sweden. sven.nelander@uu.se.

journal_articles.title: Longitudinal single-cell profiling of breast tumors highlights immune and epigenetic mechanisms associated with sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors.
journal_articles.abstract: Estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer treatment is based primarily on endocrine therapy. To dissect mechanisms of sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors in ER-positive breast cancer, we profiled tumor biopsies from 25 patients during neoadjuvant therapy using single-cell RNA sequencing, immune receptor sequencing and enhancer activity mapping. Malignant cells with high ER signaling and elevated activity of enhancers with ER binding sites were sensitive to treatment. Resistance was associated with androgen receptor signaling, dedifferentiation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Poor responders preferentially used the androgen receptor cis-regulome under treatment pressure. The baseline tumor microenvironment was associated with tumor downstaging. Poor responders exhibited a 'hot', yet ineffective immune landscape enriched for naive lymphoid and undifferentiated myeloid cells. Good responders showed an active immune microenvironment with sustained clonal expansion of T cells. Our longitudinal single-cell analyses elucidate the genetic, cellular and epigenetic mechanisms driving sensitivity and resistance to neoadjuvant aromatase inhibition in ER-positive breast cancer.

last_author.name: Xavier Tekpli
last_author.affiliation: Department of Medical Genetics, Oslo University Hospital, Oslo, Norway. xavier.tekpli@medisin.uio.no.

journal_articles.title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children's everyday speech.
journal_articles.abstract: Children learn to understand and speak from the speech around them, yet how that everyday input shapes learning remains unresolved. Large language models show that language is learnable from data, but their scale and training conditions differ sharply from a child's natural experience. We trained cognitively feasible, child-specific models on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1000 days of life. Each model learned incrementally from a single child's ordered speech input without prior linguistic knowledge, developing phoneme-like and word-form representations that tracked each child's learning pace. Learning was dependent on dense daily sampling and replay of recent input, indicating that both experience- and memory-related processes are necessary. These findings show that everyday experience contains sufficient structure for language learning and establish child-specific modeling for testing developmental theories.

last_author.name: Uri Hasson
last_author.affiliation: Princeton Neuroscience Institute, Princeton University, Princeton, NJ, USA.

journal_articles.title: Exosome secretion is required for Sonic Hedgehog dispersal and signal gradient formation in the embryonic limb bud mesenchyme.
journal_articles.abstract: Carrier-assisted diffusion and cytoneme transport help disperse Hedgehog morphogens across diverse embryonic tissues, yet their relative contributions to patterning mesenchymal tissues remain poorly understood. Here, we combine signaling assays with quantitative microscopy to establish exosome secretion as a major mechanism for Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) dispersal. Using a synchronous release system to visualize Shh trafficking, we demonstrate that Shh traffics through the exosome biogenesis pathway in limb bud mesenchymal cells. Shh-bound exosomes diffuse through extracellular space and also bind and travel along cytonemes, providing two alternative modes of transport. We show that exosome secretion is essential to establish short-range Shh signaling gradients in vitro and contributes to shaping Shh protein gradients in the limb bud in vivo. We propose that exosome-based Shh secretion, combined with different modes of extracellular transport, provides a tunable mechanism to sculpt Shh gradients across different length and time scales.

last_author.name: Edwin Munro
last_author.affiliation: Department of Molecular Genetics and Cell Biology, University of Chicago, Chicago, IL, USA. Electronic address: emunro@uchicago.edu.

journal_articles.title: A single-cell atlas of pediatric undifferentiated recurrent fever reveals candidate immune regulators.
journal_articles.abstract: Children with periodic fever syndromes not attributable to infections, rheumatic disorders, malignancies, or known monogenic autoinflammatory conditions are classified as "syndrome of undifferentiated recurrent fever" (SURF). To date, treatment remains empirical, often resulting in only a partial response, underscoring the unmet clinical need for new therapeutic strategies. To advance the molecular understanding of SURF, we generated a large-scale single-cell RNA-seq immune atlas of 29 SURF patients with more than 200,000 cells. Comparison of patients with three healthy cohorts revealed large-scale metabolic shifts together with a distinct cytokine signature already observable during afebrile periods. This indicates that afebrile SURF cannot be considered a less inflammatory resting state but rather as a distinct homeostatic state. Furthermore, our analysis suggests an NAMPT-mediated autocrine feedback loop connecting the metabolic dysregulations with the pro-inflammatory phenotype in monocytes. This study offers insights into the SURF immunopathology and generates testable hypotheses to guide future therapies.

journal_articles.title: Cell size asymmetry regulates neural stem cell proliferation and lineage expansion in the Drosophila brain.
journal_articles.abstract: Asymmetrically dividing invertebrate and vertebrate stem cells can produce unequal sibling cell sizes but the function of cell size asymmetry (CSA) remains underexplored. Here, we use Drosophila neural stem cells (NSCs) to investigate how changes in CSA affect cell fate decisions and neurogenesis. Using live-cell imaging, NSC lineage analysis, and gene expression profiling, we find that altering CSA expands the NSC pool but restricts lineage expansion. Ordinary differential equation (ODE) models suggest two possible mechanisms: NSC volume sensitivity and NSC self-inhibition. Consistent with the volume-sensitivity model, the NSC growth regulator Imp and the G1-S cell-cycle regulator CycE are upregulated in NSCs with altered CSA. In addition, the differentiation factor Prospero is asymmetrically inherited in symmetrically dividing NSCs, suggesting a mechanism for NSC self-inhibition. Together, our results suggest that cell size and cell fate determinants regulate NSC proliferation lineage expansion and progeny differentiation in the developing Drosophila brain.

last_author.name: Clemens Cabernard
last_author.affiliation: Department of Biology, University of Washington, Seattle, WA 98105, USA. Electronic address: ccabern@uw.edu.

journal_articles.title: Sex-biased enhancers shape transcriptional sex differences across human tissues.
journal_articles.abstract: Sex differences influence human physiology and disease susceptibility, yet the regulatory mechanisms underlying sex-biased transcription remain unclear. Here we present eModule, which quantifies enhancer RNA (eRNA) transcription from Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) RNA-seq data to identify sex-biased active enhancers across 41 human tissues. We find that 47% of transcriptionally active enhancers are sex-biased in at least one tissue. These enhancers are tissue-specific, often organized into super-enhancers with chromatin signatures, and associated with rewiring of transcription factor (TF) regulatory networks. Evolutionary analyses reveal that many sex-biased enhancers are primate-specific and derived from transposable element (TE) exaptation, with contributing TE families enriched for binding sites of sex-associated TFs. Sex-biased enhancers also harbor variants linked to traits with sex differences and are inferred to regulate therapeutic target genes. Our findings position sex-biased enhancer activity as a regulatory layer shaping sex-biased transcription, with implications for regulatory evolution, GWAS interpretation, and sex-informed precision medicine.

last_author.name: Bingsen Chen
last_author.affiliation: College of Biological and Food Engineering, Guangdong University of Petrochemical Technology, Maoming 525000, China.

journal_articles.title: The YAP/TAZ-Tgfbr2-stiffness feedback loop governs divergent cell fates of muscle-resident mesenchymal progenitors.
journal_articles.abstract: Mesenchymal progenitors are essential for muscle regeneration, but also contribute to fat accumulation and fibrosis. Several extrinsic and intrinsic factors regulating adipogenic or fibrogenic differentiation of mesenchymal progenitors have been identified. However, it remains unclear how different cues are integrated to determine cell fate. Here, we demonstrate that interstitial stiffness and the mechanosensitive hippo pathway regulate mesenchymal progenitor cell fate. Fat accumulation model reduced interstitial stiffness and nuclear YAP/TAZ-positive mesenchymal progenitors compared with a regeneration model, whereas YAP/TAZ deficiency in mesenchymal progenitors enhanced fat deposition. Mechanistically, YAP/TAZ induced expression of the anti-adipogenic genes Aldh1a2 and Wnt5a, and the pro-fibrogenic gene Tgfbr2, which mediates TGF-β binding. Loss of Tgfbr2 in mesenchymal progenitors reduced transient collagen deposition, decreased stiffness, and increased fat accumulation during regeneration. We propose a stiffness-YAP/TAZ-Tgfbr2-collagen regulatory loop governing mesenchymal progenitor cell fate and highlight its importance for optimal muscle regeneration.

last_author.name: So-Ichiro Fukada
last_author.affiliation: Laboratory of Stem Cell Regeneration and Adaptation, Graduate School of Pharmaceutical Sciences, The University of Osaka, Suita, Osaka, Japan. Electronic address: fukada@phs.osaka-u.ac.jp.

journal_articles.title: An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction.
journal_articles.abstract: RNA language models have achieved strong performance across diverse downstream tasks by leveraging large-scale sequence data. However, RNA function is fundamentally shaped by hierarchical structure, making structural information important for pre-training. Existing approaches often depend on noisy annotations or task-specific objectives that can limit generalizability. Here we present structRFM, a structure-guided RNA foundation model trained on 21 million RNA sequence-structure pairs by integrating base-pairing interactions into masked language modelling through a pair-matching operation. We also introduce MUSES, a multi-source ensemble of secondary structures designed to mitigate predictor bias, and a dynamic masking ratio that balances structure-guided and nucleotide-level masking. structRFM learns joint sequence and structure representations as sequence-level, nucleotide-level and pairwise features for broad downstream adaptation. It ranks highly in zero-shot homology classification and establishes new benchmarks for secondary-structure prediction. Its tertiary-structure adaptation, Zfold, consistently improves both three-dimensional predictions and their extracted secondary structures, with performance comparable to AlphaFold31 across CASP15-natural, CASP16 and RNA-Puzzles. structRFM also improves performance on function-prediction tasks and generalizes to newly released RNA families and long non-coding RNAs. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of structure-guided pre-training and highlight multimodal RNA language models for robust structural and functional inference. The complete 21-million-pair dataset, model weights and source code are openly available to support multimodal RNA foundation-model development.

last_author.name: S Kevin Zhou

journal_articles.title: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism.
journal_articles.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heritable, and mutations in hundreds of genes have been implicated as individually rare causes of ASD1-3. Understanding how disruptions to these functionally diverse genes lead to the core features of ASD remains a major challenge4. Moreover, ASD is three- to four-fold more common in male than in female individuals5, and female autistic people tend to carry more autosomal risk alleles for ASD compared with their male counterparts6,7; however, the biological basis of this 'female protective effect' (FPE) has remained unknown8,9. Here we show that individual perturbations of 18 ASD genes in human neural progenitor cells converge on shared effects on gene expression, including widespread downregulation of other ASD genes. De novo reconstruction of a gene regulatory network enabled identification of central transcriptional regulators that drive this transcriptomic convergence, including prominent ASD gene CHD8 and candidates including REST. Furthermore, X-linked transcription factor ZFX, which is expressed from both the active and the inactive X chromosomes in female individuals10, emerged as a key activator of many ASD genes: we propose that the higher ZFX expression level observed in the female brain can buffer damaging mutations in diverse ASD genes, contributing to the female protective effect. Together, these results show how key gene regulatory networks can become broadly and similarly dysregulated upon disruption of individual ASD genes and provide molecular insight into the female protective effect in ASD.

last_author.name: Christopher A Walsh

journal_articles.title: Bromide-mediated enhancement of far-UVC/peracetic acid process for selective micropollutant abatement.
journal_articles.abstract: Far‑ultraviolet 222 nm (UV222) effectively activates oxidants to degrade organic micropollutants (OMPs) in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), but its synergy and ecotoxicity with bromide (Br-) are unclear. This study investigates the synergy of peracetic acid (PAA) and Br- by UV222 (UV222-PB) for OMPs degradation. The system's fluence-based rate constant for model pollutants (0.0159 cm2·mJ-1) is 3.01 and 15.74 times that of UV254-PB and UV365-PB. Radical and theoretical analyses show that far‑ultraviolet strengthens the interaction between PAA and Br-, prolongs radical chains, and boosts organic radicals and reactive bromine species, dominating electron‑rich OMPs oxidation. Correlations of ln(kobs) with vertical ionization potential and highest occupied molecular orbital energy for 10 OMPs confirm selective oxidation. UV222-PB performs robustly in various water matrices and shows low ecotoxicity in assays such as seed germination and zebrafish embryo. Life cycle assessment confirms its sustainability. These findings offer insights and guidance for UV222-based AOPs in brominated water treatment.

last_author.name: Xiaofei Tan

journal_articles.title: Claudin-2 protects from enteropathogenic E. coli-infection and colitis by promoting crypt fetalization via β1-integrin/FAK/YAP signaling.
journal_articles.abstract: Citrobacter rodentium (Cra) infection, a murine model of enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (EPEC) infection, induces crypt proliferation that potentially promotes mucosal healing and pathogen clearance, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Cra infection upregulates claudin-2 (CLDN2), which has been proposed to facilitate pathogen clearance by enhancing Na⁺ flux and diarrhea. However, CLDN2 is dispensable for intestinal Na⁺ homeostasis. Here, we investigate whether Cra-induced CLDN2 protects against Cra-infection and colitis by regulating crypt proliferation. Using mice with intestinal epithelial-specific CLDN2 overexpression or deletion (Cldn2KO), we evaluate the role of CLDN2 in Cra colonization, inflammation, and epithelial regeneration. Organoid cultures assess epithelial-intrinsic mechanisms, while co-immunoprecipitation identifies CLDN2-associated signaling complexes. CLDN2 overexpression protects against Cra colonization and colitis, whereas Cldn2KO mice exhibit increased bacterial burden, exacerbated inflammation, and impaired crypt proliferation. Mechanistically, CLDN2 promotes crypt fetal-like reprogramming (fetalization), which is suppressed in Cldn2KO mice. Inhibiting EGFR-activation abolishes CLDN2 induction and phenocopies Cldn2KO phenotype. Furthermore, CLDN2 promotes FAK and YAP activation by stabilizing the β1-integrin-FAK complex, thereby driving crypt fetalization. Collectively, these findings identify CLDN2 as a critical regulator of mucosal defense and epithelial regeneration through activation of the β1-integrin-FAK-YAP signaling axis, beyond its classical role in paracellular ion permeability.

last_author.name: Amar B Singh
last_author.affiliation: Department of Medicine, Division of Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Motility; The University of Kansas Medical Center, Kansas City, KS, USA. asingh10@kumc.edu.

journal_articles.title: Embryonic origin of cancer in newborn twins.
journal_articles.abstract: Studying monozygotic twins who present with identical cancers informs on the developmental origins of childhood tumours. Here, we perform whole genome sequencing on multiple tumour, normal, and placental samples to reconstruct the phylogeny of a soft tissue cancer that spread in utero between monozygotic twins. We demonstrate the origin of the tumour from one twin and time its diversification and transplacental spread to the other twin, showing that the spread occurred only once. This generalisable and scalable approach additionally allows us to dissect the earliest stages of twinning, revealing unexpected asymmetrical contributions of embryonic lineages to the placenta and each twin and challenging the classical model of twinning.

last_author.name: Sam Behjati
last_author.affiliation: Wellcome Sanger Institute, Hinxton, UK. sb849@medschl.cam.ac.uk.

journal_articles.title: Quantitative changes in 3D contact predict changes in enhancer-promoter regulation upon cohesin depletion.
journal_articles.abstract: Enhancers are drivers of gene regulation thought to act via 3D interactions with promoters. However, genome-wide cohesin depletion causes only limited changes in gene expression, despite widespread loss of contact domains, raising questions about how 3D contacts and cohesin influence enhancer function. Here, we introduce CRISPRi of regulatory elements upon degron operation (CRUDO), to quantitatively assess how changes in contact frequency affect enhancer-driven gene regulation. We analyzed 1039 candidate enhancers near five cohesin-dependent genes and identified 30 significant enhancer-gene pairs, 16 with cohesin-dependent effects. While all cohesin-dependent enhancers were distal (>50 Kb), not all distal enhancers were sensitive to cohesin. Instead, changes in enhancer effects correlated with changes in enhancer-promoter 3D contact frequency, which appeared to depend on both genomic distance and other locus-specific factors. Across the genome, most predicted enhancer-gene regulatory interactions do not show substantial contact changes upon cohesin depletion, explaining why only a small subset of genes are cohesin-sensitive. Together, our results illuminate how 3D contacts tune enhancer effects on endogenous gene expression.

last_author.name: Jesse M Engreitz
last_author.affiliation: Department of Genetics, Stanford University School of Medicine, Stanford, CA, USA. engreitz@stanford.edu.

journal_articles.title: The Wnt co-receptor Arrow-LRP5/6 is required for planar cell polarity establishment in Drosophila.
journal_articles.abstract: Wnt-signaling, via β-catenin or the planar cell polarity (PCP) branch, is crucial for development, tissue homeostasis, and linked to many diseases. LRP5/6, arrow/arr in Drosophila, is the obligate co-receptor in Wnt/β-catenin signaling, with ligand binding to a Frizzled (Fz) family member and LRP5/6. Current models for Wnt/PCP signaling omit Arr-LRP5/6 and PCP is presumed functioning without these co-receptors. Here we show that arr-LRP5/6 is fully required in Wnt/PCP signaling. In Drosophila, loss of arr results in aberrant PCP mediated cellular orientation and loss of polarity coordination in wings, comparable to core PCP factors mutations, with defects manifest as loss of asymmetric PCP factor localization and reduced levels of Dishevelled (Dsh) with centrally forming wing hairs. In the eye, arr mutant tissue displays phenotypes with defects in chirality and photoreceptors R3 and R4 cell fates. Functional interactions indicate that Fz can recruit Arr, and Arr potentiates Fz-Dsh PCP signaling in all tissues tested. Furthermore, arr-LRP5/6 sensitizes the ligand pair Wg, Wnt4 with the receptor fz, and the core PCP factors fmi and Vang/stbm to cause PCP defects in heterozygous conditions. Our data support a core PCP function of Arr-LRP5/6, promoting Wnt/Fz-Dsh PCP-complex activity.

last_author.name: Marek Mlodzik
last_author.affiliation: Department of Cell, Developmental, & Regenerative Biology, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, NY, USA. marek.mlodzik@mssm.edu.

journal_articles.title: A nematic framework for sprouting angiogenesis.
journal_articles.abstract: Sprouting angiogenesis is critical for embryogenesis, wound healing, and tumor growth. Here, we show that the liquid crystal framework, which has recently been leveraged to study various morphogenetic events, provides unique insight into angiogenic sprouting. In response to vascular endothelial growth factor, a potent proangiogenic factor, endothelial cells cultured on the surfaces of soft collagen hydrogels form elongated cell streams that coexist with more polygonal cell regions. Angiogenic sprouting initiates preferentially at cell stream tips, where nematic order gradients are most pronounced. We demonstrate that cell streams are associated with large traction forces that lead to three-dimensional deformations of the underlying hydrogel and that stream formation results from a delicate balance between microtubule polymerization and actomyosin contractility. Last, we show that active control of nematic order allows modulation of sprout formation, highlighting the key role of endothelial cell orientation gradients in angiogenic sprouting and paving the way for new therapeutic avenues.

last_author.name: Abdul I Barakat
last_author.affiliation: LadHyX, CNRS, Ecole Polytechnique, Institut Polytechnique de Paris, Palaiseau, France.

journal_articles.title: Common transcriptional changes in the brain during hibernation and Alzheimer's disease.
journal_articles.abstract: Hibernation demands rapid brain adaptations, involving cycles of reduced metabolic rate during torpor, followed by brief periods of arousal. Previous studies show hibernation induces a drastic increase in Tau hyperphosphorylation, but a mechanistic connection to disease remains unclear. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing on hippocampi of golden hamsters, we unveil large transcriptional shifts across the hibernation cycle in all cell types, especially glia. Common transcriptional changes in mitochondrial and ribosomal genes are observed in all different cell types. In addition, hibernation triggers an inflammatory-like response in microglia that in part resembles cell states observed in Alzheimer's disease, but here in the absence of Aβ-accumulation and neurodegeneration. These findings reveal brain transformations that might help preserve vital functions under extreme conditions and they suggest that early cellular changes in AD may be a natural adaptive process.

last_author.name: Patrik Verstreken
last_author.affiliation: VIB-KU Leuven Center for Neuroscience; Leuven, Belgium.

journal_articles.title: Decoder-FFPE-seq enables sensitive, genome-wide spatial transcriptomics of archival tissues at single-cell resolution.
journal_articles.abstract: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue-compatible spatial transcriptomics (ST) is transforming biology and histopathology, but achieving high sensitivity, genome-wide coverage, single-cell resolution, and researcher accessibility remains challenging. To address these challenges, we here present a dendrimeric DNA coordinate barcoding design for FFPE tissue-adapted spatial RNA sequencing (Decoder-FFPE-seq) by integrating RNA-to-DNA probe conversion with blotting-assisted barcoding. Decoder-FFPE-seq provides single-cell resolution with a >2.6-fold sensitivity increase in whole-transcriptome mouse brain and archived human sample profiling over existing platforms, resolving potential cellular identity of low-abundance genes, finer tissue architecture, and capturing an epithelial-mesenchymal transition-associated signature for prognostic value. With expanded probe libraries, Decoder-FFPE-seq captures long noncoding and viral RNAs, revealing their spatial coregulatory networks with messenger RNAs in oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCCs). In an OSCC immunotherapy cohort, two CD8+ T cell subpopulations were respectively identified in pre- and postchemoimmunotherapy samples, potentially linked to treatment response. Decoder-FFPE-seq establishes a robust, high-resolution, and accessible framework for sensitive ST profiling of archival tissues in fundamental and translational studies.

last_author.name: Chaoyong Yang
last_author.affiliation: Institute of Molecular Medicine, Shanghai Key Laboratory for Nucleic Acid Chemistry and Nanomedicine, Department of Urology, Department of pathology, Renji Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, Shanghai 200127, China.

journal_articles.title: Fluid-driven robotic micromanipulation for assembloid fabrication.
journal_articles.abstract: The assembly of cellular spheroids into spatially organized assembloids represents a transformative paradigm for modeling complex biological systems. However, the lack of standardized fabrication strategies fundamentally limits the precision and reproducibility of these models, hindering their widespread application. Here, we present a robotic micromanipulation platform-Fluid-Driven Tweezer with Visual Servo Control (FDT-VSC). By integrating multidimensional visual perception with microfluidic control, our system enables the gentle and programmable assembly of diverse cellular spheroids. Leveraging this platform, we achieve the bottom-up construction of structurally defined, heterogeneous multicellular tissues, and the programmed orchestration of multilineage models that recapitulate the complex microenvironments of early organogenesis. Crucially, the system improves consistency during the scalable fabrication of tumor-stroma assembloids, supporting reliable drug screening. These results demonstrate that FDT-VSC advances assembloid-based applications across modular tissue engineering, developmental biology, and drug discovery.

last_author.name: Huijun Gao
last_author.affiliation: Research Institute of Intelligent Control and Systems, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, China.

journal_articles.title: PDS5A and TOP2B cooperate for chromatin recruitment via CTCF.
journal_articles.abstract: PDS5A, a cohesin regulatory subunit, and topoisomerase IIB (TOP2B), an enzyme resolving DNA topological problems, interact with CTCF and regulate transcription and genome organization. We ascertained that PDS5A and TOP2B are recruited to CTCF-bound chromatin cooperatively and that catalytically active TOP2B increases PDS5A occupancy genome wide. Notably, the amino-terminal 95 to 116 amino acids of CTCF interacts with PDS5A, giving rise to CTCF-PDS5A-TOP2B interaction in vitro and to PDS5A chromatin enrichment via active TOP2B in vivo. PDS5A-TOP2B function together in moderating the resultant gene expression and genome organization. Loss of CTCF (95 to 116 amino acids) led to dysregulated gene expression and mildly reduced chromatin loops. In gliomas, PDS5A and TOP2B expression levels vary, but correlate, contributing to distinctive gene expression patterns. Inducible PDS5A knockdown led to reduced TOP2B occupancy and altered gene expression. Furthermore, PDS5A mediated sensitivity to TOP2 cancer drugs in glioma cells. This functional interaction between PDS5A and TOP2B at CTCF boundaries expands upon the mechanisms affecting gene regulation through genome organization, with implications for glioma therapeutics.

last_author.name: Danny Reinberg
last_author.affiliation: Howard Hughes Medical Institute, University of Miami, Miami, FL 33136, USA.

journal_articles.title: Age-dependent structural evolution of a functional amyloid contributes to memory impairment in Drosophila.
journal_articles.abstract: Cryogenic electron microscopy has revealed endpoint structures of ex vivo amyloid filaments, but how amyloids assemble and evolve in living organisms-and how these transitions affect physiology-remains poorly understood. Here, we map the age-dependent structural landscape of Orb2 amyloid, a synaptic translation regulator required for long-term memory, across the adult lifespan of Drosophila melanogaster. By determining multiple Orb2 amyloid structures, we uncover a dynamic, age-linked progression of amyloid states. Translation-promoting assemblies predominate early in life, whereas aging shifts the Orb2 amyloid ensemble toward structurally distinct, destabilization-resistant assemblies with reduced translational activity, coinciding with memory impairment. Manipulating memory-related chaperones in the brain shifts Orb2 toward youthful, translation-promoting states and improves memory in old flies; conversely, shifting Orb2 toward aged-like, translation-deficient states in young adults is associated with premature memory impairment. These findings define an in vivo trajectory of amyloid evolution and link amyloid structural dynamics to synaptic translation and memory.

last_author.name: Ruben Hervas
last_author.affiliation: School of Biomedical Sciences, The University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, HKSAR, China; School of Biomedical Engineering, The University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, HKSAR, China. Electronic address: ruhm@hku.hk.

journal_articles.title: CRISPR mutagenesis of the MYC locus reveals a druggable ultraconserved RNA element.
journal_articles.abstract: Noncoding sequences comprise most of the human genome; however, their functional significance remains largely elusive. Using CRISPR tiling mutagenesis with near-PAMless, high-fidelity SpRY-Cas9, we mapped the fitness landscape of an entire human gene, the 10-kb MYC locus, at base-pair resolution. This unbiased interrogation revealed that 67% of functionally essential base pairs are noncoding. Essential noncoding base pairs are under strong constraint in the human population but show limited evolutionary conservation across species. Within this landscape, we identified an ultraconserved noncoding RNA element in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) that promotes perinuclear localization of MYC mRNA and nuclear localization of MYC protein through interaction with hnRNP L. Steric-blocking antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) targeting this element selectively eliminate diverse MYC-dependent cancer cells and inhibit growth of patient-derived tumor organoids. Together, these findings establish noncoding sequences as major carriers of functional genetic information and identify a therapeutically actionable RNA element whose targeting disrupts MYC-driven cancer.

Electronic address: xuebing.wu@columbia.edu.

journal_articles.title: A hierarchical regulatory cascade programs chlamydospore formation in the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys flagrans.
journal_articles.abstract: Chlamydospores provide durable stress tolerance for fungal survival and enable shelf-stable biocontrol agents, yet their genetic regulation in fungi remains poorly understood. Here, using the nematode-trapping fungus Arthrobotrys flagrans as a model, we define a hierarchical regulatory cascade for chlamydospore formation. LaeA mediates H3K9 monomethylation to license this developmental program. Furthermore, we identify VeA and Ste12 as LaeA partners, and the importin KapA as a nuclear gatekeeper. This upstream module activates VosA/VelB, which induces AbaA/StuA to control the effectors ChsG, McdD, and McdD-modified glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored proteins for chlamydospore cell wall biogenesis. The expression levels of regulators within this regulatory cascade (LaeA/VeA/Ste12-VosA/VelB-StuA/AbaA-ChsG and McdD) determine chlamydospore yield and convert environmental cues into differentiation. This framework guides strain engineering for high-yield chlamydospore production and suggests a regulatory paradigm potentially conserved across fungi.

journal_articles.title: Clusterin, through exercise-mediated liver-heart crosstalk, promotes heart regeneration after myocardial infarction.
journal_articles.abstract: Loss of cardiomyocytes drives cardiac remodeling and ultimately leads to heart failure, highlighting the need to promote cardiac regeneration. Exercise has been known to enhance cardiac repair and stimulate cardiomyocyte proliferation; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we demonstrated that exercise-induced exerkine clusterin mediates the pro-regenerative effects of running plasma on cardiac repair and cardiomyocyte proliferation following myocardial infarction (MI). Cardiac-specific Clu knockout attenuated, whereas clusterin overexpression enhanced, post-MI cardiac regeneration. Recombinant clusterin administration promoted heart regeneration in adult mice after MI. Mechanistically, clusterin activated NF-κB via proteasome-dependent IκBα degradation through direct binding with IκBα. Furthermore, the liver was identified as the major source of exercise-induced circulating clusterin; hepatocyte-specific Clu knockdown abolished the stimulatory effect of exercise plasma on cardiac regeneration. This study reveals a liver-heart crosstalk mechanism by which exercise-induced clusterin promotes cardiomyocyte proliferation, positioning clusterin as a potential therapeutic target for post-MI heart failure.

journal_articles.title: Hyperosmotic stress induces rewiring of 3D chromatin interactions.
journal_articles.abstract: Cells continually face environmental stressors that challenge homeostasis, yet how three-dimensional (3D) chromatin structure contributes to these stress responses remains unclear under hyperosmotic conditions. To investigate this, we map 3D chromatin structure, its molecular drivers, and transcriptional outcomes during sorbitol-induced hyperosmotic stress. Within 1 hour of sorbitol treatment, pre-existing loops and domains collapse, while several hundred de novo sorbitol-induced loops emerge. These loops are punctate, longer-range, and transient. 3D chromatin structure largely returns to baseline conditions by 24 hours. Loop reorganization is consistent across cell types and hyperosmotic stimuli. Sorbitol-induced loops require cohesin but not CTCF, and anchors are enriched at active promoters harboring GC-rich transcription factor motifs. Genes at these anchors show delayed activation following loop formation, consistent with loops acting upstream of transcription. Together, hyperosmotic stress triggers rapid, reversible, CTCF-independent chromatin reorganization that correlates with transcriptional adaptation.

journal_articles.title: Intermittent fasting enhances muscle regeneration via an EDA2R-NIK-myomixer axis.
journal_articles.abstract: Skeletal muscle exhibits a remarkable regenerative capacity that relies on adult stem cells known as satellite cells (SCs), which differentiate into myogenic progenitors to drive muscle repair. How varying energy availability alters myogenesis, however, remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that intermittent fasting (IF) in mice upregulates a myogenic gene program, including Myomixer, a muscle-specific fusogen that facilitates the merging of progenitor cells into myofibers. IF enhances the regeneration of injured muscles by expanding the SC population and promoting the proliferation and fusion of myogenic progenitors. These effects are absent in an SC-depletion model. We show that fasting-induced EDA2R-NIK signaling increases Myomixer expression and fusion in myoblasts. Notably, mice lacking EDA2R or NIK fail to respond to the myogenic effects of IF. Furthermore, our data suggest that mice with Duchenne muscular dystrophy also benefit from an IF regimen. Therefore, IF-induced regeneration holds potential for aiding recovery from muscle damage.

journal_articles.title: Single-cell and spatial characterization of the human pancreas in cystic fibrosis.
journal_articles.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) causes severely damaged pancreatic morphology and cystic fibrosis-related diabetes (CFRD), but the cellular drivers of CFRD in the pancreas are not understood. Here, we perform single-cell and spatial profiling of 2.04 M cells from 23 non-disease or CF pancreas donors. A high-mucin ductal sub-type had relatively preserved abundance and genomic profiles but altered localization in CF. Changes in inflammatory and fibrotic pathways were driven by crosstalk between immune and pro-fibrotic cells in specific niches. Beta cells had extensive changes in CF, including increased stress responses and evidence for compensatory secretion, that were distinct from those in type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Islets localized near large adipose tissue and collagen in CF had reduced beta cells linked to signaling from adipocytes, macrophages, stellate cells, and high-mucin ductal cells. Overall, our results highlight pancreatic microenvironments of beta cell dysfunction in CF and offer in-roads to preserving beta cells in CFRD.

journal_articles.title: Transcriptional and functional profiling reveals a dynamic continuum of beta-cell activation states.
journal_articles.abstract: A central question is whether beta-cells respond uniformly to glucose. Using phospho-S6 as an activation marker, this study shows that beta-cells are recruited sequentially as glucose concentrations increase. Recruitment is spatially organized, with high-threshold cells predominantly located in the islet core. Transcriptomic profiling indicates functional heterogeneity among beta-cells. A low-threshold subset is characterized by enhanced stress resilience necessary for sustained secretion. An intermediate subset, enriched for calcium-signaling and vesicle-excitatory genes, modulates postprandial glucose excursions. The high-threshold subset specializes in high-capacity protein synthesis and insulin secretion to manage glucose peaks. Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals that these functional subsets form a continuous spectrum rather than discrete subpopulations. This division of labor is adaptable; under high-fat diet-induced metabolic demand, islets undergo remodeling with a global reduction in activation thresholds and a shift toward high-capacity profiles. Collectively, these findings identify a beta-cell hierarchy that balances metabolic resilience with secretory demand to maintain glucose homeostasis.

journal_articles.title: Stem cell turnover constrains somatic mutational diversity in plants.
journal_articles.abstract: Plants continuously generate new organs throughout their lifetime, a process that relies on a small population of stem cells located at the center of the shoot apical meristem (SAM). These cells self-renew and produce descendants that are displaced to the SAM periphery, where they contribute to organ formation and differentiation. Although the population is maintained over time, stochastic or biased turnover can lead to the dominance of specific lineages. Because de novo somatic mutations are inherited along cell lineages, these dynamics are expected to play a central role in shaping the accumulation and distribution of within-plant somatic genetic variation. In this Hypothesis, we discuss the mechanisms underlying stem cell behavior, and hypothesize that stem cell turnover reduces genetic diversity within the SAM over developmental timescales. We also develop a mathematical model linking stem cell turnover to somatic mutation accumulation and predict that this reduction arises because higher turnover limits the co-existence of independent stem cell lineages. Finally, we outline how lineage tracking and somatic DNA sequencing could be used to test these predictions in vivo.

journal_articles.title: Translation of a small upstream open reading frame functions as a rheostat for the regulation of lin-41 by the Let-7 microRNA in Caenorhabditis elegans.
journal_articles.abstract: MicroRNAs often exert modest effects on target protein levels yet play essential roles in development. How microRNA function combines with other regulatory mechanisms to control dosage-sensitive targets remains incompletely understood. In Caenorhabditis elegans, the Let-7 microRNA represses translation of its principal developmental timing target, the LIN-41 TRIM-NHL RNA-binding protein, by binding two complementary sites in the lin-41 3'UTR and recruiting the microRNA-induced silencing complex (miRISC) to repress translation. Here we identify an independent layer of translational repression in somatic cells that is mediated by a 5' regulatory exon containing a seven-amino-acid upstream open reading frame (uORF) and conserved sequence elements. Genome editing indicates that the specific uORF amino acid sequence is not required; instead, our data suggest that uORF translation and 5'UTR structure limit initiation at the downstream lin-41 start codon. Together with Let-7, the 5' regulatory exon and its embedded uORF provide multitiered control of lin-41 translation, which limits LIN-41 to levels compatible with normal somatic development.

journal_articles.title: Microcephaly-causative ASPM mutations disrupt mitotic spindle orientation and timely specification of human outer radial glia cells.
journal_articles.abstract: Mutations in the gene abnormal spindle-like, microcephaly-associated (ASPM) are the most common cause of primary microcephaly (MCPH). The mechanisms underlying MCPH have remained unclear, as ASPM disruption leads to species-specific phenotypes. Using human cortical organoids, we observed premature mitotic spindle randomization in ASPM-mutant ventricular cortical progenitors, followed by their early delamination to the basal compartment. Similar delamination following mitotic spindle misorientation could be induced by overexpression of Inscuteable, further linking the two phenotypes. Delaminated progenitors resembled outer radial glial cells (oRGCs), which are selectively amplified in human corticogenesis, but they failed to adopt a bona fide oRGC identity, displaying downregulation of key oRGC genes required for their amplification and maintenance. Our findings link the evolutionarily conserved requirement of ASPM for proper mitotic spindle orientation to the species-specific timing of delamination and proper specification of human oRGC, shedding light on the origins of species-specific vulnerability to ASPM mutations.

journal_articles.title: VAPA-dependent lipid transport at ER-lamellar body contact sites promotes human lung surfactant formation.
journal_articles.abstract: Vesicle-associated membrane protein-associated proteins (VAPs) establish membrane contact sites (MCS) between the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and other organelles through interactions with FFAT-containing proteins, coordinating lipid synthesis, transfer, and metabolism. Their tissue-specific functions remain poorly understood. We report a patient with a homozygous nonsense variant in VAPA (p.(Glu12∗)), presenting with profound global developmental delay and progressive surfactant dysfunction leading to cholesterol pneumonitis and pulmonary fibrosis. Alternative translation initiation partially bypasses the premature stop codon, producing an N-terminally truncated VAPA protein with impaired FFAT binding capacity and disrupted lamellar body (LB) formation in human alveolar type 2 cells. We identify the pulmonary disease-associated ATP-binding cassette transporter A3 (ABCA3), a regulator of surfactant lipid accumulation, as a VAPA interactor. VAPA-ABCA3 interaction facilitates lipid exchange at previously uncharacterized ER-LB MCSs, a function lost upon VAPA truncation. Our findings establish VAPA-dependent MCS dysfunction as a mechanism of syndromic lung disease and define a pathway for surfactant lipid trafficking.
