journal_articles.title: Ecological and social cues orchestrate concerted courtship in Drosophila.
journal_articles.abstract: Mating decisions are often attributed to the sensory signalling between prospective sexual partners. Yet these interactions are also shaped by the broader environmental context in which they unfold, to appropriately align sexual arousal with reproductive opportunities1-6. Here we show that in Drosophila erecta mating is strictly contingent on the ecological and social environment generated as flies densely aggregate in groups on a food patch. We find that food volatiles directly promote male sexual arousal, triggering individuals to sample and pursue potential mates, giving rise to dynamic interactions across the group. The ensuing visual motion transforms each male's visual field, which in turn further amplifies his arousal, generating a multisensory feedback loop that coordinately promotes courtship across individuals. D. erecta's strict dependence on environmental cues appears latent in related species, such as Drosophila melanogaster, where food odour can promote arousal7 but is dispensable for vigorous courtship. Comparative circuit analyses show that species-specific thresholds for sexual arousal reflect variation in how olfactory input modulates conserved nodes controlling courtship drive, rendering food volatiles a strict sensory gate only in D. erecta. Together, our findings highlight how environmental cues not directly tied to sexual signalling can profoundly influence reproductive behaviour and reorganize the social landscape to ensure mating occurs in contexts where reproductive opportunities are abundant.

journal_articles.title: In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs.
journal_articles.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, but its efficacy remains limited by multiple negative regulatory mechanisms intrinsic to T cells1-4. Here we perform a high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout (DKO) CRISPR screen, and identify multiple DKO gene pairs that are both effective and synergistic. The top pair, NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO, has multiple favourable immunological features. Whole-transcriptome profiling and in vivo single-cell RNA sequencing reveal that NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO specifically upregulates metabolic pathways in CAR-T cells, which show significantly higher metabolic fitness and mitochondrial activity. NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO CAR-T cells and T cells exhibit exceptionally potent antitumour efficacy and long-term tumour control across different tumour models without compromising safety features. NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO outperforms several benchmark single-gene and dual-gene modifications in T cells and CAR-T cells5-9. These data demonstrate high-throughput in vivo CAR-T DKO screening for rapid discovery of combination targets, and establish NR4A1-SOCS3 as a promising pair of intracellular checkpoints to engineer high-performance CAR-T therapies against cancer.

journal_articles.title: Microbiome-wide PheWAS links gut microbial SNVs to health and exposures.
journal_articles.abstract: Alterations in the microbial composition of the human gut have been associated with a wide range of chronic diseases1,2. Yet species-level composition alone can obscure extensive within-species genetic diversity and functional variation. This has driven a shift towards strain-resolved, genetic-level analysis of the microbiome, leveraging microbial genetic variation to identify disease-relevant genes and pathways3-6. Here we conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) analysing 12.8 million gut microbial single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) with 244 host health phenotypes and environmental exposures in 10,781 individuals from 6 independent cohorts. We identify 940 independent associations across 69 host factors, including age, sex and cardiovascular and metabolic parameters. Structural analyses identified host-phenotype-associated SNVs in functionally important regions of proteins, findings that inform mechanistic hypotheses about how microbial genetic changes relate to environmental and host physiological factors. For example, we identified an age-associated SNV in Faecalibacterium prausnitzii that affects an amino acid within the protein pocket that binds glutathione. To support future efforts, all study summary statistics are provided in an online catalogue ( https://fulab.web.rug.nl/SNV-MWAS/ ). Together, these results identify new biological connections between the human host and microbial genetic variants at base pair resolution and provide a resource for hypothesis generation that will aid future understanding of the strain-level functionality of the gut microbiota.

journal_articles.title: Phase separation of SMARCAL1 orchestrates epigenetic reprogramming and methionine metabolism to foster radioresistance and immunosuppression.
journal_articles.abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation has emerged as a key mechanism governing cellular organization and function, but its role in pathological processes and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely elusive. Here we show that SMARCAL1 forms nuclear condensates via liquid-liquid phase separation to enhance histone H4 lactylation and chromatin accessibility. This SMARCAL1‑driven epigenetic reprogramming not only facilitates the recruitment of DNA repair proteins, leading to radiotherapy resistance, but also regulates methionine adenosyltransferase transcription, thereby promoting the methionine cycle and inducing T cell exhaustion and immune therapy tolerance. Intriguingly, SMARCAL1 is identified as a biomarker for predicting therapy response and patient stratification. Importantly, pharmacological disruption of SMARCAL1 condensates by digoxin sensitizes tumours to both radiotherapy and anti-PD1 therapy in multiple models. These findings highlight the crucial role of condensates centred on SMARCAL1-histone H4 in governing DNA repair and immune microenvironment remodelling, as well as propose an innovative strategy to overcome radioimmunoresistance.

journal_articles.title: 3D Reconstruction of Dinoflagellate Chromosomes from Hi-C Data Challenges the Cholesteric Liquid Crystal Hypothesis.
journal_articles.abstract: Dinoflagellates have permanently condensed chromosomes that are often described as cholesteric liquid crystals (CLCs). The CLC model proposes that DNA is organized into parallel fibers within stacked discs, such that the fiber orientation rotates between adjacent discs. Extrachromosomal loops extending from the discs are hypothesized to be more accessible and thus to contain transcriptionally active genes. Although the CLC model captures some features of dinoflagellate chromosome structure, its validity has not been rigorously tested against modern genomic data. Here, we use chromatin conformation capture (Hi-C) data to simulate 3D conformations of chromosome scaffolds for three dinoflagellate species: Fugacium kawagutii, Symbiodinium microadriaticum, and Breviolum minutum. Consensus and population-based modeling generate diverse polymer conformations with moderate orientational and nematic order. However, we find no evidence of cholesteric discs. Moreover, contact probability curves from empirical Hi-C data are inconsistent with the CLC model. Nevertheless, we show that introducing locus-specific boundaries into CLCs can produce simulated Hi-C contact maps with topologically associating domains (TADs), which are observed experimentally for these species. Finally, by mapping RNA-seq data onto our simulated conformations, we find no enrichment of transcriptional activity at the chromosome periphery. Our results challenge the long-standing CLC model and suggest that dinoflagellate chromosomes are organized into condensed structures with local but not global order that does not impede transcription.

journal_articles.title: A model of brain function to predict tau across Alzheimer's disease and related disorders.
journal_articles.abstract: We developed a machine learning framework grounded in a computational model of brain function and FDG-PET imaging to predict Alzheimer's disease (AD)-type tau across AD and related disorders (ADRD). The model was trained on 1088 research participants spanning normal aging and ADRD with FDG-PET and flortaucipir-PET (FTP-PET). Validation was conducted in: (1) a longitudinal subset of the training cohort (n = 215), (2) Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (n = 295), and (3) a heretogeneous clinical cohort (n = 264; n = 28 with FTP-PET). Results showed that the model accurately predicted FTP-PET when applied at the participant-level (R2 ~ 0.34-0.71). It performed well in clinical scenarios, including classification of low versus high tau stages (79-95% accuracy) and prediction of tau in a heterogeneous clinical cohort without FTP-PET. These findings advance the understanding of the relationship between neurodegeneration and AD-type tau and provide a framework for estimating AD-type tau across ADRD.

journal_articles.title: A multi-center, single-arm, phase 2 trial of dasatinib in T follicular helper cell lymphomas.
journal_articles.abstract: T follicular helper cell lymphomas (TFHL) harbor activating T cell receptor (TCR) signaling mutations and epigenetic alterations, such as TET2 mutations. Here, we conduct a multi-center, single-arm, phase 2 trial of the tyrosine kinase inhibitor dasatinib in patients with relapsed/refractory TFHLs (jRCT2031190079). The primary outcome is the overall response rate (ORR) according to CT-based Lugano criteria 2014. Key secondary endpoints include ORR in RHOA-mutated patients and progression-free/overall survival. The main inclusion criteria consist of TFHL diagnosis and relapse following at least 1 prior chemotherapy regimen. Key exclusion criteria encompass central nervous system involvement, history of other malignancies, and receipt of chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 4 weeks. Nineteen patients are enrolled, with 18 receiving dasatinib and 17 evaluable for efficacy. Median age is 73 years, 50% are female, and angioimmunoblastic T cell lymphoma is the predominant subtype (n = 13). Dasatinib yields a 23.5% ORR, below the prespecified 30% endpoint. Treatment-related adverse events occur in 61.1% of patients (n = 11). Patients harboring TCR signaling mutations, especially those with RHOA p.G17V, achieve a 36.4% ORR, whereas no responses are observed in mutation-negative cases. Exploratory single-cell RNA sequencing reveals interferon-γ/tumor necrosis factor-enriched tumor microenvironments and peripheral expansion of cytotoxic T cell clones in responders. Conversely, early progression correlates with a high TET2 mutation burden in non-malignant immune cells, including CD8+ T cell subsets. While the primary outcome is below the prespecified endpoint, our exploratory findings implicate immune dysfunction involving TET2 mutations in limiting the therapeutic benefit of dasatinib.

journal_articles.title: AI-accelerated scalable synthesis of nanocrystals for cost-effective photovoltaics.
journal_articles.abstract: Metal halide perovskite nanocrystals (PNCs) are promising candidates for next-generation optoelectronics. However, their commercial application necessitates low-cost synthesis and processing methods that surpass conventional lab-scale techniques. To address this, we report a ligand triggered room-temperature injection (LTRI) method that initiates nanocrystal nucleation by tuning precursor reactivity with addition of short-chain octanoic acid (OcA). Subsequently, integrating automation synthesis and machine learning, we further develop an efficient AI-accelerated framework towards fast and target synthesis of the FAPbI3 (FA: formamidinium) PNCs. Leveraging machine learning modeling, we identify that the critical size and distribution of FAPbI3 PNCs can be effectively optimized by tuning the feed ratio of OcA to the precursor formamidinium acetate. Furthermore, our LTRI method is fully compatible with flow-synthesis system for scale-up production, enabling a substantial reduction in production cost to US$2.16 g-1, significantly lower than the widely adopted hot-injection method (US$118.81 g-1). For practical application, we achieve a power conversion efficiency of 19.37% in photovoltaic applications with significant enhancement in device stability, matching the highest reported results for nanocrystal-based solar cells.

journal_articles.title: Antimicrobial peptides derived from Nemuri induce ribosomal condensation to inhibit translation.
journal_articles.abstract: Antibiotic resistance is a global health threat requiring antimicrobials with alternative modes of action. Growing evidence indicates that bacteria organize key intracellular processes through biomolecular condensates and other forms of spatial organization, yet whether such spatial organization can be exploited as an antimicrobial target remains unclear. Here, we identify intrinsically disordered antimicrobial peptides, generated from the Drosophila sleep-inducing protein Nemuri, that inhibit bacterial growth by targeting ribosomal organization. Mechanistically, these peptides enter bacterial cells without overt membrane disruption and accumulate in ribosome-rich regions, where they bind broadly to RNA and ribosomal surfaces through multivalent interactions. This engagement remodels ribosome-rich regions into condensates with reduced ribosomal mobility, thereby suppressing global protein synthesis and distinguishing these peptides from canonical site-specific ribosome-targeting antibiotics. Furthermore, Nemuri-derived peptides exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, including activity against drug-resistant pathogens, with low cytotoxicity toward Drosophila and mammalian cells. Together, our findings identify the organization and material dynamics of bacterial ribosomes as a biophysical vulnerability that can be exploited by antimicrobial peptides, revealing how a naturally evolved metazoan host-defense system turns intracellular organization itself into an antibacterial target.

journal_articles.title: Cep57 organizes pericentriolar material through dual architectural modules and prevents human mosaic variegated aneuploidy.
journal_articles.abstract: Mosaic variegated aneuploidy (MVA) is a developmental disorder associated with chromosome segregation defects. Mutations in the centrosomal protein Cep57 cause MVA2 syndrome, yet the molecular basis of Cep57 function has remained unclear. Here, using MINFLUX nanoscopy, structural biology, biochemical approaches, and analyses of patient-derived cells, we show how Cep57 organizes the inner pericentriolar material (PCM) to support centriole biogenesis. We show that Cep57 acts as a molecular bridge between centriolar microtubules and the PCM through two architecturally distinct interactions. Its oligomeric C-terminus anchors to centriolar microtubules, whereas its dimeric N-terminus engages Cep63 through a conserved bundle-like interaction, thereby linking the Cep63-Cep152 platform to the centriole and recruiting Plk4 and other components required for procentriole formation. Analysis of primary T lymphocytes from MVA2 patients carrying the Cep63-binding-defective CEP57∆exon 3 mutation reveals a predominant centriole-duplication defect accompanied by minor centriole amplification, likely resulting from disorganized PCM-induced premature centriole disengagement. Our findings show Cep57 as a central architectural organizer that couples centriolar microtubules to the molecular machinery driving centriole biogenesis, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding centrosome dysfunction and aneuploidy-associated diseases.

last_author.name: Kyung S Lee
last_author.affiliation: Cancer Innovation Laboratory, National Cancer Institute, National Institutes of Health, Bethesda, MD, USA. kyunglee@mail.nih.gov.

journal_articles.title: Characterization of chemoresistant cell populations improves risk stratification and therapy prediction in pediatric acute myeloid leukemia.
journal_articles.abstract: Most pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (pAML) patients achieve complete remission after chemotherapy, yet nearly 40% ultimately relapse and die from their disease. High risk cases are typically referred for stem cell transplantation (SCT) in first remission, but because SCT is associated with substantial toxicity and cures after relapse are rare, accurate risk prediction is critical. Here, we show that combining the detection of chemoresistant cell populations, inferred from single-cell transcriptomic profiles of paired diagnosis-relapse samples, and cytogenetic biomarkers at diagnosis with measurable residual disease after induction chemotherapy, substantially improves risk prediction. This approach identifies a patient subgroup comprising 20% of the patients who do not undergo SCT, with a 5-year event-free survival below 40%, and accounting for nearly half of all deaths in this population. Molecular characterization of these cell populations reveals therapeutic vulnerabilities and potential targeted treatment strategies for high-risk pAML, providing a framework for precision oncology diagnosis and intervention.

last_author.affiliation: Texas Children's Cancer Center, Baylor College of Medicine, Houston, TX, USA. sumazin@bcm.edu.

journal_articles.title: Clock neurons modulate seizure timing through a diurnal switch.
journal_articles.abstract: People with epilepsy experience daily oscillations in seizure risk. Using a video-tracking model to automate detection, we explored mechanisms underlying spontaneous seizures in Drosophila and find that flies, like people, exhibit daily oscillations in seizure risk. These rhythms are absent in flies lacking a molecular circadian clock and are independent of sleep. Thermogenetic screening and cell-specific clock perturbations reveal that the ventrolateral neurons, including "morning cells", and dorsolateral neurons, comprising the "evening cells", modulate diurnal oscillations in seizure risk. Pigment-dispersing factor and short neuropeptide F from morning cells increase seizure risk during the day. During this time, morning cell activity increases whole-brain activity. At night, morning cells switch to glycine signaling likely acting on evening cells to decrease seizure risk. Optogenetic inhibition of clock neurons suppresses seizure risk. Our findings reveal an unexpected role for brain clock neurons in modulating daily seizure risk.

last_author.name: Amita Sehgal
last_author.affiliation: Howard Hughes Medical Institute, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, PA, USA. amita@pennmedicine.upenn.edu.

journal_articles.title: Deep-learning single-cell profiling uncovers interbacterial and drug-driven reshaping of pathogen virulence.
journal_articles.abstract: Bacterial invasion and genotoxicity are key contributors to infectious disease progression and carcinogenesis. Yet current methods do not quantify these processes systematically and at single-cell resolution, limiting our ability to explore how interplay of virulence factors and drug effects shape pathogenicity. Here, we present MALVINA, a high-throughput deep-learning workflow integrating host-pathogen co-culture and high-content imaging to jointly measure bacterial invasion and host DNA damage. Applied to Escherichia coli isolates and human colorectal epithelial cells, we demonstrate MALVINA's versatility by deciphering (1) strains with elevated invasive or genotoxic potential, (2) interbacterial modulation of virulence, (3) pro-virulent drug effects, (4) virulence-targeting drugs, and (5) bacterial potentiation of drug toxicity. MALVINA revealed strain-specific virulence profiles and colibactin-dependent suppression of competitors' invasion coupled with enhanced genotoxicity. It also enabled identification of drug-induced modulation of bacterial invasion and genotoxicity, offering a new perspective for virulence-aware drug profiling. Overall, MALVINA offers an adaptable framework for dissecting pathogen-host-drug interactions.

journal_articles.title: Domino effect enables dynamic electronic structure evolution for stable and efficient water purification.
journal_articles.abstract: The purification of water contaminated by persistent organic pollutants remains a critical global challenge, largely due to the intrinsic trade-off between high catalytic activity and long-term stability in advanced oxidation processes. Despite the tremendous potential of single-atom catalysis, its traditional static design strategies cannot adapt to dynamic and multi-step reactions. Here, we break the limitation of this static design by reporting a domino catalysis within a heteronuclear MgCo dual-single-atom catalyst. In this system, the Mg site selectively photoreduces O2 to H2O2 under light irradiation. This in-situ generated H2O2 and its derived surface hydroxyl groups act as dynamic modulators, progressively tailoring the electronic structure of the adjacent Co site. This on-demand electronic refinement optimally lowers the energy barriers for subsequent peroxymonosulfate activation and radical desorption, thereby driving efficient pollutant degradation while intrinsically stabilizing the Co center against leaching. Experiments and theoretical calculations elucidate that this seamless and spatially ordered cascade avoids competitive adsorption and maximizes efficiency. The system exhibits the highest normalized rate constant of 595.3 min-1 M-1 among various refractory contaminants over thirty regeneration cycles, outperforming the most state-of-the-art catalytic systems. This work introduces a dynamic and self-evolving catalytic approach that breaks the traditional activity-stability trade-off, suggesting a potential pathway toward effective and sustainable water purification technologies.

last_author.name: Shuangshi Dong
last_author.affiliation: Key Laboratory of Groundwater Resources and Environment (Jilin University), Ministry of Education, Jilin University, Changchun, China. sdong@jlu.edu.cn.

journal_articles.title: Electronically tuned N-terminal glycine selective bioconjugation enables in vitro and in vivo species-specific Staphylococcus aureus targeting.
journal_articles.abstract: Precisely targeting a biomolecule within living systems could create unique opportunities at the biology-medicine interface. Such methods have been non-trivial due to the complex selectivity attributes. Here, we introduce an electronically tunable chemical technology that targets N-terminal glycine, a unique low-frequency molecular signature. Initially, we established the method using peptides and proteins, along with mechanistic insights. The reactivity, selectivity, and bioconjugate stability remain unaffected by diverse bioadditives. These unique attributes enable the selective targeting of the pentaglycine-based molecular signature in Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus), a leading contributor to bacterial infection-associated mortality. Notably, the method facilitates species-specific detection of S. aureus and its resistant strains. It enables late-stage bond-engineering to install multiple biorthogonal handles, downstream chemistry, and chemically orthogonal reversal. The specificity extends to in vivo labeling of S. aureus within Drosophila melanogaster, as well as skin, tissue, and blood infections in mice. The N-terminal glycine modification inhibits drug-susceptible and drug-resistant clinical strains of S. aureus, including biofilm formation and preformed biofilms. Finally, the in vivo efficiency is established using a wound-healing assay in mice. The exclusive N-terminal glycine residue-specific targeting across the molecular complexity spectrum, both in vitro and in vivo, establishes peptidoglycan as a potential diagnostic and therapeutic target.

last_author.name: Vishal Rai
last_author.affiliation: Department of Chemistry, Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Bhopal, Bhauri, Madhya Pradesh, India. vrai@iiserb.ac.in.

journal_articles.title: Game theory driven multi-agent framework mitigates language model hallucination.
journal_articles.abstract: Lightweight large language models hold promise for scientific applications but remain limited in rule-constrained domains because they can reproduce linguistic patterns without following scientific principles, leading to hallucinations. Here, we show that G-Frame, an adaptive multi-agent framework inspired by Bayesian game and team game principles, enables a closed-loop process for automated data generation, model evaluation, and training. By assigning complementary roles to multiple agents, G-Frame generates structured reasoning data and constructs a specialized corpus containing 363,045 chain-of-thought examples and 199,589 question-answer pairs. Using this corpus together with domain pre-training and adaptive training, the 7-billion-parameter model OmniChem achieves competitive performance across the reported benchmarks and reduces the ChemJudge hallucination rate from 41.95% for the base model to 12.91%. Case studies further illustrate potential applications in molecular design and selected synthesis-planning tasks. These results support G-Frame as an extensible game theory-driven multi-agent framework for improving the reliability of lightweight scientific language models.

last_author.name: Shengyang Tao
last_author.affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Fine Chemicals, Frontier Science Center for Smart Materials, Dalian University of Technology, Dalian, China. taosy@dlut.edu.cn.

journal_articles.title: Generative design of high-fidelity microstructures using physics-aware machine learning.
journal_articles.abstract: Generative models are increasingly being applied in materials science to enable materials design. However, generating out-of-distribution microstructures with high fidelity that satisfy multiple target properties remains a major challenge. Here, we present a physics-aware generative-optimization strategy for the inverse design of microstructures, guided by mutually exclusive properties. The approach integrates interfacial and crystallographic information directly into the loss function of surrogate models, together with introducing a latent-space sampling scheme that balances microstructural diversity with physical realizability. We demonstrate the framework using a small yet diverse alloy dataset comprising well-characterized microstructures and tensile stress-strain responses. By targeting strength-ductility synergy, the generated out-of-distribution microstructures exhibit substantially improved fidelity, particularly in their interfacial features. The produced microstructures are validated by crystal plasticity finite element simulations and experiments. We attribute the enhanced mechanical performance to the emergence of a bimodal grain-size morphology absent from the training data. Our results demonstrate a data-efficient strategy for high-fidelity microstructure design that leverages interfacial physics to achieve multiple properties synergy.

last_author.name: Ruihao Yuan
last_author.affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Solidification Processing, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi'an, China. rhyuan@nwpu.edu.cn.

journal_articles.title: Genetic variants associated with cell-type-specific intra-individual gene expression variability reveal mechanisms of genome regulation.
journal_articles.abstract: Gene expression varies substantially across cells, even within seemingly homogeneous populations. Understanding how genetic variation influences this variability is critical for elucidating mechanisms of genome regulation, yet the genetic control of cell-to-cell expression variability remains poorly characterised. Here, we introduce MEOTIVE (Mapping genetic Effects On inTra-Individual Variability of gene Expression), a statistical framework that identifies genetic effects on gene expression variability (sc-veQTLs) while modelling mean-variance dependence. Applying MEOTIVE to single-cell RNA-seq data from 1.2 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells across 980 donors in the OneK1K cohort, we identify 14-3,488 genes with significant sc-veQTLs across blood cell types, including 2,103 shared across multiple cell types. We further detect 55 SNP-gene pairs (34 genes) associated with gene expression dispersion (sc-deQTLs), enriched for immune and viral response pathways; 32 of these associations remain significant after additional adjustment for mean expression. Notably, rs1131017 in the 5'UTR of RPS26 is associated with widespread expression dispersion across cell types and reduced autoimmune disease risk. We also identify a monocyte-specific deQTL in LYZ (rs1384), which replicates in an independent cohort. MEOTIVE provides a robust framework for mapping the genetic regulation of gene-expression variability at single-cell resolution and reveals pathways linking cellular heterogeneity to autoimmune disease risk.

last_author.name: Joseph E Powell
last_author.affiliation: Garvan-Weizmann Centre for Cellular Genomics, Garvan Institute of Medical Research, Sydney, NSW, Australia. j.powell@garvan.org.au.

journal_articles.title: High-resolution binding data of TFIID and cofactors show promoter-specific differences.
journal_articles.abstract: TFIID is instrumental in recognizing promoter sequences and initiating transcription, yet a cohesive understanding of how this complex engages and functions at different promoter types in vivo is still lacking. Here, we employed ChIP-nexus to capture high-resolution binding footprints of all Drosophila TFIID subunits across the genome. These footprints reveal TFIID sub-modules whose DNA contacts agree with cryo-EM structures and point to new structural details. At different promoter types, the footprints of the TAFs are very similar, suggestive of the same engaged TFIID conformation. In contrast, the binding profile of TBP is promoter-specific, enabling us to identify TATA, DPR, and TCT/housekeeping promoters de novo, along with their underlying core promoter elements. Notably, TATA promoters display specific TBP and NC2 binding footprints and reduced TAF occupancy, consistent with a fraction of transcripts being initiated in a TAF-independent manner at these promoters in vivo. Together, our results provide a comprehensive resource for linking structural and biochemical results to in vivo data and offer a potential explanation for the increased burst size observed at TATA promoters.

last_author.name: Julia Zeitlinger
last_author.affiliation: Stowers Institute for Medical Research, Kansas City, MO, USA. jbz@stowers.org.

journal_articles.title: HuBMAP Data Portal: a resource for multimodal spatial and single-cell data of healthy human tissues.
journal_articles.abstract: The NIH Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP) Data Portal ( https://portal.hubmapconsortium.org/ ) serves as a comprehensive repository for multimodal, multi-scale spatial and single-cell data from healthy human tissues. As of August 2026, the portal hosts 9,316 public datasets from 26 data types spanning 29 organ classes across 501 donors. Portal infrastructure and user interfaces support data search and discovery, visualization, and analysis directly in web browsers. These capabilities include metadata- and data-driven search, collaborative Workspaces with access to high-performance compute, and interactive Vitessce visualizations across non-spatial, 2D, and 3D spatial datasets. Data-type-specific uniform processing pipelines and rigorous quality control processes ensure comparability of results across laboratories, organs, and donors, while externally processed community-contributed datasets provide complementary perspectives. Here we describe portal functionality, infrastructure, and design, and highlight its role as a platform for large-scale spatial single-cell research across diverse data types, organs, and scales.

last_author.name: Nils Gehlenborg
last_author.affiliation: Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA. nils@hms.harvard.edu.

journal_articles.title: Neonatal overfeeding accelerates age-related sarcopenia and metabolic disorders through lifelong gut mucosa and microbiota programming in mice.
journal_articles.abstract: Early-life nutrition shapes lifelong health, yet the long-term consequences of childhood overnutrition, particularly on musculoskeletal aging, remain unclear. Here, we show that neonatal overfeeding acts as a developmental insult that accelerates age-related sarcopenia in both sexes. Using different mouse models, early overnutrition shortens lifespan and exacerbates late-life muscle atrophy, accompanied by metabolic dysfunction. Mechanistically, neonatal overfeeding disrupts goblet cell development, leading to persistent mucus barrier defects and consequently reduced Akkermansia muciniphila (A. muciniphila) colonization during aging. Fecal microbiota transplantation transfers the sarcopenic phenotype, implicating gut dysbiosis in disease propagation. Loss of A. muciniphila reduces acetate production, impairs muscle mitochondrial function at least in part via suppressed GPR43 signaling, and aggravates sarcopenia. Conversely, A. muciniphila reconstitution or acetate supplementation restores mitochondrial homeostasis and improves muscle performance in aged mice. These findings reveal a developmental origin of age-related sarcopenia and define a gut-muscle axis linking early-life overnutrition to muscle aging, highlighting the preventive potential of optimizing early nutrition to support healthy aging.

last_author.name: Cen Xie
last_author.affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Drug Research, Shanghai Institute of Materia Medica, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai, China. xiecen@simm.ac.cn.

journal_articles.title: Next-generation functional diagnostic paradigm for musculoskeletal diseases based on live SWIR imaging.
journal_articles.abstract: The pursuit of accurate diagnosis for musculoskeletal diseases has driven significant advancements in imaging technologies. However, fully understanding the complexity of the diseases requires monitoring multiple functional components, particularly during locomotion. Here, we present a live short-wave infrared (SWIR) imaging strategy designed to capture functional variations of musculoskeletal diseases in male murine models, and further extend it to male rabbit models and human knee joint. This approach directly visualized the kinematics of synovial fluid during normal locomotion, identifying distinct peak of fluid flow. When applied to injury evaluation, it revealed significant kinematic differences in patellar maltracking between isolated tendon injuries and combined tendon and muscle injuries, providing mechanical insights into their long-term outcomes. The versatility of this technique was further demonstrated by simultaneously examining bone and vascular kinematics during bone healing. This enabled the monitoring of large arteries in bone, and revealed an initial divergence from the bone regeneration. Overall, this advanced live SWIR imaging methodology enables dynamic, motion-robust, and multi-componential assessments of functional variations, positioning it as a next-generation functional diagnostic tool for musculoskeletal diseases.

last_author.name: Jun Chen
last_author.affiliation: Department of Sports Medicine, Huashan Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai, China. biochenjun@fudan.edu.cn.

journal_articles.title: PSHIC reveals allele-specific chromatin organization by phasing-free structural modeling.
journal_articles.abstract: Resolving the distinct 3D chromatin architectures of parental chromosomes is critical for understanding diploid genome function, but many haplotype-resolved Hi-C contact-map methods remain constrained by their reliance on phased single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). This dependency treats reconstruction as a simple tag-and-sort problem, leading to massive data loss, extreme fragility to phasing errors, and inapplicability in SNP-sparse contexts. We introduce PSHIC, a computational framework that reveals this hidden chromatin organization by employing phasing-free structural modeling, directly from aggregated Hi-C data. PSHIC models chromosomes as continuous manifolds and solves the inverse problem of finding two homolog-specific structures whose combined contacts best explain the observed data. Comprehensive simulations across varying sequencing depths, SNP densities, and phasing error rates demonstrate that PSHIC consistently outperforms established methods, achieving superior accuracy (SCC ≥ 0.987), loop detection (F1≥ 0.952), and structural fidelity (DER ≤ 0.04). Applications to real human and mouse Hi-C datasets show that PSHIC recovers known allele-associated features in X-chromosome inactivation, genomic imprinting, and regulatory networks. Results align with orthogonal experimental approaches including 3D DNA-FISH, 4C-seq, and ChIA-PET. PSHIC democratizes diploid chromatin analysis by enabling robust reconstruction in non-model organisms and other SNP-limited or poorly phased contexts.

last_author.name: Shuaicheng Li
last_author.affiliation: Department of Computer Science, College of Computing, City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China. shuaicli@cityu.edu.hk.

journal_articles.title: Plasma radicals control synthesis of platinum supported on nitrogen-doped graphitic carbon for ambient-pressure ammonia synthesis.
journal_articles.abstract: Integrating isolated metal atoms and subnanometer clusters within highly doped, structurally ordered carbon frameworks remains challenging because thermal synthesis promotes dopant loss, metal migration, and structural disorder. We report a biphasic liquid-liquid solution plasma strategy that produces nitrogen-doped graphitic carbons with a record-high nitrogen content of 22.4 atomic% while stabilizing atomically dispersed platinum sites and subnanometer clusters. Analysis of 53 cyclic organic precursors by optical emission spectroscopy and machine learning identifies CN and C2 radicals as positive descriptors for nitrogen incorporation and graphitic ordering, whereas Hβ emission correlates with hydrogen termination and disorder. In ambient-pressure nonthermal plasma-assisted ammonia synthesis, this material used as a catalyst achieves 3.97 gNH3 kWh‒1 and sustained operation for 85 h without degradation. Infrared spectroscopy, isotope-switching experiments, and density functional theory are consistent with a proposed cooperative catalytic pathway involving nitrogen activation at isolated platinum sites, hydrogenation at platinum clusters, and a Mars-van Krevelen-like contribution from Pt-Nx-C motifs.

last_author.name: Sibudjing Kawi
last_author.affiliation: Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, National University of Singapore, Singapore, Singapore. chekawis@nus.edu.sg.

journal_articles.title: Saturation mutagenesis enables RAD51D clinical variant interpretation and identifies distinct biochemical functions.
journal_articles.abstract: The tumor suppressor RAD51D is essential for homologous recombination (HR). Pathogenic variants in RAD51D are associated with breast and ovarian cancers. However, most clinical missense variants are of uncertain significance. Here, we report a multiplex assay of variant effect to test 6,888 RAD51D coding variants for loss-of-function. The resulting variant-to-function map perfectly separates known pathogenic and benign variants and is validated by orthogonal HR and biochemical assays across 70 clinical variants. Our screen shows that variants in the DNA-binding or ATPase core most severely compromise HR, and we identify the RAD51D-RAD51C interface within the BCDX2 complex as essential for regulating its ATPase activity. We hypothesize that, paradoxically, the primary function of RAD51D is to slow the ATPase activity of BCDX2, thereby allowing sufficient time and space for RAD51 filament assembly. Together, we identify hotspots of deleterious RAD51D variants and uncover the mechanisms by which variants compromise its biochemical functions.

last_author.name: Kara A Bernstein
last_author.affiliation: Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics, University of Pennsylvania Perelman School of Medicine, Philadelphia, PA, USA. Kara.Bernstein@Pennmedicine.upenn.edu.

journal_articles.title: Synthetic lethal screens reveal p300/CBP as a vulnerability for GNAQ-driven uveal melanomas.
journal_articles.abstract: Uveal melanoma is the most common intraocular cancer in adults, driven by activating mutations in GNAQ or GNA11, which encode the G proteins Gαq and Gα11. Currently, therapeutic options for uveal melanoma, particularly metastatic uveal melanoma, remain limited. Through an isogenic CRISPR screening approach, we identify EP300, which encodes the protein lysine acetyltransferase p300, as a top synthetic lethal vulnerability in the context of GNAQ mutation. Notably, CREBBP, which encodes the closely related paralogue CBP, also emerges among the top-ranked candidates. Mechanistically, we find that p300 and CBP support YAP-dependent transcription downstream of oncogenic Gαq in uveal melanoma through interactions with YAP at chromatin. These interactions enhance H3K27 acetylation at the promoters and putative enhancers of YAP target genes and promote the recruitment of RNA polymerase II and CDK9. Using multiple in vivo models representing clinically relevant stages of Gαq-mutant uveal melanoma, we find that p300 inhibition, by both genetic and pharmacological approaches, profoundly impairs tumor growth and metastasis. Taken together, this study establishes p300 as a potential therapeutic target for Gαq-driven uveal melanoma, which is dependent on unrestrained YAP signaling.

last_author.name: Le Yu
last_author.affiliation: Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of New Drug Screening, School of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, P. R. China. yulezy@smu.edu.cn.

journal_articles.title: Systematic screen of RNA binding proteins that enhance circular RNA translation.
journal_articles.abstract: Translatable circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional mRNA therapy due to their improved stability that results in a prolonged expression window. The translation of circRNAs is mainly driven by internal ribosome entry site (IRES) or IRES-like elements, which is tightly regulated by various trans-acting RNA binding proteins (RBPs). Here we develop a cell-based system to systematically screen RBPs that enhance translation of circRNAs, identifying 68 proteins as putative activators of noncanonical translation. These translation activators are involved in a broad range of biological processes including RNA processing, ribosomal biogenesis, and translation initiation. We further design a machine learning algorithm to extract common sequence features of these activators and predict more potential RBPs with translation activator activities. The newly identified and predicted activators are subsequently validated to promote the IRES-mediated circRNA translation in a context-dependent fashion. Overall, this study provides new insights into IRES-related trans-acting factors and expands the toolbox for engineered RBPs in RNA synthetic biology.

last_author.name: Zefeng Wang
last_author.affiliation: Shanghai Institute of Nutrition and Health, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai, China. wangzf@sustech.edu.cn.

journal_articles.title: The CCCH-type zinc-finger PfMD3 promotes translation for malaria parasite transmission.
journal_articles.abstract: Sexual maturation and fertility of the malaria-causing parasite, Plasmodium spp., are critical to transmission between hosts. This developmental process involves an intricate gene expression regulatory network that drives gametocyte commitment, development, and the production of male and female gametes. Here, we characterize the role of the CCCH-type zinc-finger protein Plasmodium falciparum Male Development 3 (PfMD3) in the formation of gametes. Genetic disruption of PfMD3 reveals a male fertility defect that decreases infectivity to mosquitoes. Molecular characterization of PfMD3 reveals its binding to mRNA transcripts is associated with male gamete development through a specific RNA sequence. Gametocyte proteins encoded by these PfMD3-bound transcripts decrease significantly in PfMD3 knockout parasites, suggesting that PfMD3 impacts translation. In addition to RNA-binding, PfMD3 also interacts with proteins involved in mRNA processing and nuclear export that influence translational regulation. This study establishes PfMD3 as an RNA-binding protein that impacts lineage-specific translation and male gamete fertility.

last_author.name: Heather J Painter
last_author.affiliation: Laboratory of Mucosal Pathogens and Cellular Immunology, Division of Bacterial, Parasitic, and Allergenic Products, Office of Vaccines Research and Review, Center for Biologics Evaluations and Research, Food and Drug Administration, Silver Spring, MD, USA. Heather.Painter@fda.hhs.gov.

journal_articles.title: Untargeted screening of drug-like compounds using high-throughput metabolomics uncovers inhibitors of key biological pathways.
journal_articles.abstract: Metabolomics has demonstrated immense potential in elucidating mechanisms of action and off-target effects of known drugs. Here, we propose that metabolomic screening of cellular response to treatment with drug-like compounds can uncover clinically relevant inhibitors - driven by the extensive catalog of metabolic pathways implicated in human diseases. We developed a high-throughput LC-MS metabolomics pipeline paired with a computational Graph Neural Network for target deconvolution, and applied it to screen a library of 1,020 drug-like compounds in cultured cells in vitro. The screen revealed four drug-like compounds targeting key disease pathways, including inhibitors of purine and pyrimidine biosynthesis and an inducer of glutathione metabolism; validated via comprehensive metabolic assessments and growth rescue experiments. In a muscle atrophy model, driven by redox imbalance, the glutathione metabolism inducer reversed atrophy markers and restored protein content. Our scalable pipeline can be readily expanded to screen thousands of compounds, paving the way for the discovery of clinically relevant metabolic inhibitors.

last_author.name: Tomer Shlomi
last_author.affiliation: Faculty of Biology, Technion-Israel Institute of Technology, Haifa, Israel. tomersh@cs.technion.ac.il.

journal_articles.title: Unveiling hidden air pollution exposure and impacts with low-cost sensor network-based frameworks.
journal_articles.abstract: India has made some progress in mitigating severe air pollution; however, many regions continue to experience fine particulate matter (PM2.5) levels exceeding World Health Organization and national standards. Despite this, local-scale exposure information beyond urban centers, intra-regional inequities, and short-term mortality impacts remain poorly understood. This study integrates dense, low-cost sensor-based PM2.5 measurements with machine learning models, recent family health survey data, and India-specific relative risk information to assess sub-regional exposure inequity among socioeconomic groups and short-term mortality impacts in Bihar, one of the most polluted and understudied states of India. Here we show a clear north-south divide in PM2.5 exposure, with northern districts having mean exposure levels 1.2 times higher. District-level mortality (per 100,000) varied up to 1.7-fold, with daily mortality showing 3.2-fold variability. We observe limited exposure inequity at the state level but substantial inter- and intra-regional inequities within Bihar.

last_author.name: Sachchida Nand Tripathi
last_author.affiliation: National Aerosol Facility, Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur, Kanpur, India. snt@iitk.ac.in.

journal_articles.title: Video-rate volumetric chemical imaging via mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography.
journal_articles.abstract: Label-free vibrational microscopy provides chemically specific access to cellular structures, yet quantitative volumetric imaging of intracellular dynamics remains challenging on subsecond timescales. Here, we demonstrate video-rate mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography (MIP-ODT) by combining high photothermal sensitivity with rapid angular scanning. The system achieves 19.2 volumes per second, nearly 400 times faster than previous MIP tomography implementations, with a signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 70 and no temporal averaging. We track lipid droplets in living cells and quantify anomalous diffusion from three-dimensional trajectories, revealing heterogeneous intracellular transport behaviors obscured in two-dimensional measurements. Rapid mid-infrared wavenumber sweeping further enables broadband multi-wavenumber volumetric chemical imaging across a 300 cm⁻¹ spectral window within 1 s. These results establish MIP-ODT as a platform for high-speed, label-free volumetric chemical imaging of single cells and quantitative investigation of dynamic intracellular organization.

last_author.name: Takuro Ideguchi
last_author.affiliation: Department of Physics, The University of Tokyo, Tokyo, Japan. ideguchi@g.ecc.u-tokyo.ac.jp.

journal_articles.title: WeedNet: a foundation model-based global-to-local AI approach for weed species identification and classification.
journal_articles.abstract: Early weed identification is crucial for effective management and control, and researchers, agronomists, and technology developers are increasingly interested in automating this process using computer vision and artificial intelligence; however, limited expert-verified data and variable morphological features have hindered the development of AI-based weed identification models. To address these issues, we present WeedNet, a global-scale weed identification model that can recognize an extensive set of weed species. WeedNet is an end-to-end weed identification pipeline that uses self-supervised learning, fine-tuning, and enhanced trustworthiness strategies. WeedNet achieved 91.02% accuracy across 1,593 weed species, with 41% of species achieving 100% accuracy. Using a fine-tuning approach, the local Iowa WeedNet model achieved 97.38% overall accuracy for 84 Iowa weeds. Testing across intra-species dissimilarity and inter-species similarity suggests that diversity in the images collected, spanning all the growth stages and distinguishable plant characteristics, is crucial in driving model performance. The global WeedNet model serves as a foundation, and the global-to-local strategy enables targeted fine-tuning to improve performance in regional weed communities. Additional validation of drone- and ground-rover-based images highlights WeedNet's potential for integration into robotic platforms. Furthermore, integration with artificial intelligence for conversational use provides intelligent agricultural and ecological conservation consulting tools for farmers, researchers, and government agencies across diverse landscapes.

last_author.name: Arti Singh
last_author.affiliation: Department of Agronomy, Iowa State University, Ames, IA, USA. arti@iastate.edu.

journal_articles.title: AI-based precision prognostics and therapy personalization for childhood brain tumors.
journal_articles.abstract: Accurate prediction of patient outcomes remains a critical challenge in oncology, in particular for childhood brain tumors, in which treatment decisions need to carefully balance risk of tumor recurrence and death against severe therapy-induced sequelae. Here, we developed MANTIS (methylation profiling and artificial neural networks for time-dependent individualized survival predictions), a precision artificial intelligence (AI) tool for medulloblastoma and ependymoma outcome prediction built on genome-wide DNA methylation array data from 2,786 patients. MANTIS generates individualized survival probabilities over a 10-year period and achieves concordance indices as high as 0.80 ± 0.07, significantly exceeding the predictive accuracy of current clinical indicators. Extending MANTIS to estimate individualized treatment effects identifies ~60% of patients with average-risk medulloblastoma without a significant survival disadvantage (P = 0.683) when treated with less intensive craniospinal irradiation doses, which is associated with improved neurocognitive outcomes. In conclusion, our study establishes a foundation for AI-based precision prognostics and therapy personalization in childhood brain tumors and offers a blueprint for similar initiatives in other cancer types.

last_author.name: Volker Hovestadt
last_author.affiliation: Department of Pediatric Oncology, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Boston, MA, USA. volker_hovestadt@dfci.harvard.edu.

journal_articles.title: Clonal hematopoiesis and cytopenias following CAR19 therapy.
journal_articles.abstract: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy (CAR19) improves survival in relapsed/refractory large B cell lymphoma compared with immunochemotherapy with intent for autologous hematopoietic cell transplantation (autoHCT). However, major toxicities include prolonged cytopenias, infection and secondary hematologic malignancies. Here, to investigate these complications, we studied patients with lymphoma receiving CAR19 and compared clinical outcomes to propensity-matched autoHCT-treated controls. CAR19-treated patients exhibited impaired immune reconstitution and increased infection. Bone marrow analysis showed that prolonged post-CAR cytopenias are associated with clonal cytopenias of undetermined significance and interferon-mediated inflammation. Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) commonly expanded following CAR19 infusion and was associated with impaired immune reconstitution and treatment-related myeloid malignancy (tMN). Post-CAR tMN was molecularly and clinically comparable to post-autoHCT tMN. Single-cell DNA analysis revealed mostly independent CH clones, while CAR integration into CH-mutant T cells occurred frequently and may drive expansion and persistence. Together, these findings implicate CH expansion and marrow inflammation in key CAR19-associated toxicities.

last_author.name: Ash A Alizadeh
last_author.affiliation: Division of Oncology, Department of Medicine, Stanford University School of Medicine, Stanford, CA, USA. arasha@stanford.edu.

journal_articles.title: Advancing morphological profiling with self-supervised learning through comparative insights into representation learning of cellular perturbations.
journal_articles.abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) enables scalable, label-free foundation models (FMs) that learn task-agnostic representations directly from images, bypassing cell segmentation and feature engineering inherent to classical morphological profiling. We present a large-scale evaluation of SSL FMs for image-based phenotypic profiling, covering contrastive (DINO), masked-based generative (MAE, iTPN) and hybrid (DINOv2) learning mechanisms, pretrained on all unannotated chemical perturbations from the Joint Undertaking for Morphological Profiling-Cell Painting (JUMP-CP) dataset (119,876 compounds, ~1.77 million images, 7 laboratories). Here we show that top-performing SSL models outperformed CellProfiler in compound-replicate retrieval on the held-out JUMP-Target2 set (302 annotated compounds, P ≤ 0.001). DINO and DINOv2 generalized across diverse perturbations and cell types, outperforming CellProfiler with 31-37% gains in site-averaged mean average precision for mechanism-of-action retrieval on EU-OPENSCREEN Bioactives (2,464 compounds), and consistently surpassing masked-based models across all benchmarks. This study provides a systematic assessment of SSL approaches for advancing morphological profiling and offers pretrained FMs to accelerate drug discovery.

last_author.name: Rui Liao
last_author.affiliation: Data Science and AI, Johnson & Johnson, Titusville, NJ, USA. RLiao2@ITS.JNJ.com.

journal_articles.title: Limitations of de novo peptide sequencing in resolving sequence ambiguity.
journal_articles.abstract: De novo peptide sequencing enables peptide identification from fragmentation spectra without relying on sequence databases. However, incomplete spectra create ambiguity, making unambiguous identification challenging. Recent deep learning advances have produced numerous de novo models that predict sequences and refine peptide-spectrum matches under such conditions. Yet, their relative strengths, weaknesses and ability to handle spectrum ambiguity remain unclear. Here we benchmark eight state-of-the-art models on three publicly available proteomics datasets, comparing performance using established metrics and quantifying inter-model agreement. We assess post-processing approaches, including iterative refinement, rescoring and reranking, for their ability to improve identification accuracy, and perform an error analysis to identify common mispredictions and their causes. Model performance varied, with considerable overlap of correct identifications. Post-processing yielded no or only modest improvements. Most sequencing errors were model-independent and driven by limited fragment ion coverage, a limitation also observed in database searches with large search spaces.

last_author.name: Tine Claeys
last_author.affiliation: VIB-UGent Center for Medical Biotechnology, Ghent, Belgium.

journal_articles.title: RobPicker: a meta-learning framework for robust identification of macromolecules in cryo-electron tomograms.
journal_articles.abstract: Accurate particle picking of macromolecules of diverse types, shapes and sizes in cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is critical for understanding the molecular architecture of biological systems in their native state. Current deep learning methods have shown potential for identifying macromolecules in tomograms; however, they are vulnerable to annotation noise in the training data and to imbalanced distributions of macromolecule species. Here, to address these limitations, we developed RobPicker, a meta-learning framework that effectively mitigates these issues by automatically learning to correct label errors and by placing greater emphasis on smaller and rarer macromolecule species. In evaluations across diverse cryo-ET datasets with noisy labels and imbalanced species distributions, RobPicker substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods, particularly in identifying small and rare macromolecules. The robustness and efficiency of RobPicker led to improved resolution in 3D density maps of protein structures, enabling high-resolution cellular structural biology analysis.

last_author.name: Pengtao Xie
last_author.affiliation: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of California San Diego, La Jolla, CA, USA. p1xie@ucsd.edu.

journal_articles.title: Spatial single-cell mapping of transcriptional differences across genetic backgrounds in mouse brains.
journal_articles.abstract: Genetic variation can alter organ structure and function. Comparative statistical analysis of organs across genetic backgrounds requires spatial, single-cell, atlas-scale data in replicates. Here we introduce atlas-scale transcriptome localization using aggregate signatures (ATLAS), a scalable tissue mapping method that learns transcriptional signatures from single-cell RNA sequencing data, encodes them in situ with tens of thousands of oligonucleotide probes and decodes them to infer cell types and imputed transcriptomes. We validated ATLAS against direct MERFISH measurements of marker genes and through quantitative comparisons to four other technologies. We profiled 40 million cells across more than 400 coronal sections from central brains of five male and five female C57BL/6J mice and five male BTBR T+tf/J mice, an idiopathic autism model. Our analysis revealed more than 40 significant differences in cell-type distributions and identified 16 regional composition changes across male-female and B6-BTBR comparisons. ATLAS thus enables systematic comparative studies, facilitating organ-level structure-function analysis of disease models.

journal_articles.title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat.
journal_articles.abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a rapidly expanding global pollutant, but its effects across biological levels from individuals to ecosystems remain unquantified. We conducted phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species with ranges that span six continents. Noise altered at least one physiological, developmental, or behavioral trait in 80% of species studied, with declines in fitness and abundance and disruptions of predator-prey interactions. Effects occurred in every habitat, although response mechanisms varied for some traits and species, creating winners and losers. Only multispecies analyses can reveal such species- and ecosystem-level impacts of anthropogenic stressors. Our results establish noise as a novel selection pressure reshaping ecosystem dynamics and as a pervasive stressor requiring soundscape protection alongside habitat conservation.

journal_articles.title: A soft wireless bioelectronic patch for noninvasive modulation of cavernosal microenvironment in diabetic erectile dysfunction.
journal_articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus-induced erectile dysfunction is difficult to reverse due to long-term impairment of cavernosal microenvironment. Conventional oral or intracavernosal injection therapies suffer from poor targeting, uneven drug distribution, and potential complications. Here, we propose a soft, wireless electronic patch for treating erectile dysfunction (SWEED) in diabetes mellitus, which enables safe, noninvasive, and controllable modulation of penile microenvironment. With its "microelectrode-drug reservoir-nanopore" configuration, SWE intensifies local electrical field nanoscopically and achieves uniform transdermal drug delivery. Through the enhanced local delivery of prostaglandin E1 (PGE1), SWEED demonstrates high efficiency in promoting the expression of vascular factors for endothelial repair and enhancing cavernosal blood perfusion. In both in vitro and in vivo settings, the platform achieves vascular regeneration and functional recovery comparable to clinical intracavernosal injection therapy. Moreover, it activates proerectile signaling pathways (EP2/PKA/CREB) and suppresses the TGF-β/Smad pathway, markedly alleviating cavernosal fibrosis. This work presents a paradigm for noninvasive diabetes mellitus-induced erectile dysfunction therapy.

journal_articles.title: BCLAF1 links RNA splicing to ATF4-dependent metabolic adaptation in acute myeloid leukemia.
journal_articles.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is driven by genetic alterations and non-mutational mechanisms that disrupt normal hematopoiesis and support leukemic cell survival. While the mutational landscape of AML is well characterized, the non-genetic processes sustaining leukemic maintenance remain less understood. Using human AML cells and murine models, we identify BCL2-associated transcription factor 1 (BCLAF1) as a key regulator of leukemic progression through control of mRNA processing. BCLAF1 physically associates with core spliceosome components and regulates alternative splicing programs in leukemic cells. Mechanistically, BCLAF1 is required for productive splicing of activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) mRNA, thereby sustaining ATF4 protein levels and downstream metabolic gene expression programs. Loss of BCLAF1 reduces ATF4 levels, leading to impaired de novo amino acid biosynthesis and increased sensitivity to venetoclax. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized mechanism linking RNA splicing control to metabolic adaptation in AML, identifying BCLAF1 as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

journal_articles.title: C:H:N:O:P stoichiometry and oxygen demand of marine organic matter are driven by phytoplankton ecophysiology.
journal_articles.abstract: Although the hydrogen and oxygen content of marine phytoplankton plays a critical role in determining oceanic O2 consumption rates, shaping habitat for anaerobic metabolism, they are often assumed to be constant in biogeochemical studies, resulting in biased estimates of respiration rates. Here, by simulating phytoplankton allocation in a general circulation model, we predict latitudinal variations in phytoplankton C:H:N:O:P composition and corresponding O2 demand. These patterns are driven by physiological adaptation to environmental conditions and are consistent with observations. Subtropical phytoplankton have more C─O bonds and lower O2 demand, as they contain more carbohydrates than higher-latitude populations. We test the sensitivity of O2 inventory and regenerated C via the biological pump (Csoft) to plausible bounds of cellular allocation and find that the global O2 inventory and Csoft decrease by ∼11 and 14%, respectively, when a cell shifts from carbohydrate-rich to protein-rich biomass. Our findings demonstrate that biochemical remodeling of phytoplankton composition mediates large-scale patterns and oceanic budgets of O2 and C.

journal_articles.title: Evidence of active whole-genome doubling (WGD) subclones in non-WGD tumors.
journal_articles.abstract: Whole-genome doubling (WGD) occurs frequently in human cancer and influences tumor evolution, metastasis, and treatment response. Here, we integrate bulk, single-cell, and spatial data to dissect the subclonal dynamics of WGD. Single-cell data analysis shows that WGD cells are prevalent even in tumors that are classified as non-WGD (nWGD). WGD subclones actively acquire somatic copy number alterations as they expand, suggesting ongoing evolution. We developed and rigorously validated a gene expression-based method, WAGES, to map WGD cell clonal fraction in bulk tumors. Applying WAGES to nWGD tumors, we reveal genomic correlates including TP53 mutations and chromosomal instability that are consistent with the presence of WGD subclones. Clinically, WAGES scores are strongly correlated with tumor metastatic potential, response to treatments including chemotherapy and immunotherapy, and patient prognosis. These findings reveal widespread WGD subclones in nWGD tumors and demonstrate their substantial impact on cancer evolution and therapeutic outcomes.

journal_articles.title: IFNAR1 stabilization sustains CD8+ T cell persistence in IFN-high colorectal cancer liver metastases.
journal_articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRC-LMs) are associated with poor survival and frequently resist immunotherapy, yet the mechanisms underlying this immune refractoriness remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify a tumor-intrinsic type I interferon (IFN-I)-high state in CRC-LMs associated with loss of the IFN-α/β receptor subunit 1 (IFNAR1) on effector T lymphocytes within immune-enriched perimetastatic niches. Reduced IFNAR1 expression stratifies patients with poor clinical outcomes. Transcriptional profiling of patient-derived organoids and complementary preclinical models revealed heterogeneous but recurrent tumor-derived IFN-I production in CRC-LMs. In IFN-Ihigh contexts, sustained signaling promoted IFNAR1 internalization on effector CD8+ T cells, impairing their persistence, survival, and effector function. Pharmacologic or genetic stabilization of IFNAR1 on cell surface restored CD8+ T cell fitness and selectively enhanced T cell receptor- and chimeric antigen receptor-based immunotherapies in IFN-Ihigh tumors. These findings define a context-dependent IFN-Ihigh / IFNAR1low axis that constrains antitumor immunity in CRC-LMs and identify IFNAR1 stabilization as a strategy to convert chronic IFN signaling from a suppressive barrier into a therapeutic vulnerability.

journal_articles.title: Local translational program at the muscle-tendon junction endows domain identity in muscle syncytia.
journal_articles.abstract: How cells establish specialized subdomains is a fundamental question in cell and tissue biology. Skeletal muscle fibers, among the largest cells in the body, are multinucleated and form distinct regions such as the neuromuscular and myotendinous junctions (MTJs), the latter forming a critical interface between muscle and tendon that transmits contractile force. While transcriptional heterogeneity among myonuclei has been described, whether local translation contributes to domain identity remains unknown, largely due to the lack of tools for domain-specific manipulation. Here, we introduce MTJ-AAV, a viral system that enables selective genetic targeting of MTJ myonuclei. This approach allowed MTJ-specific ribosome tagging and revealed extensive translational regulation underlying MTJ biology and its remodeling during exercise. Untranslated regions of these transcripts were sufficient to control regionalized translation. Notably, the Krüpper-like factor-family transcription factors emerged as translationally up-regulated targets at the MTJ, where they drive local gene expression. Our findings establish local translation as a key layer of subcellular specialization and provide a versatile toolkit for dissecting spatial molecular regulation within muscle syncytia.

journal_articles.title: Massively parallel self-assembly of suspendable microcompartments for functional cell screening.
journal_articles.abstract: Modern biology increasingly demands platforms that can compartmentalize and analyze single cells and cell-cell interactions at massive scale, yet existing compartmentalization strategies based on microfluidics suffer from critical limitations. Emerging lab-on-a-particle technologies such as nanovials enable anchored single cells or small groups of cells to be isolated and assayed in a fully suspendable and parallelized manner using standard instrumentation, although their open architectures can result in loss of growing or un-attached cells. Here, we introduce capped nanovials: self-assembling hydrogel compartments formed by docking spherical capping particles into bowl-shaped nanovials. We routinely achieve capping of >80% of all nanovials in a sample and >90% sorting yield by flow cytometry, making the capped nanovial system well-suited for preparing and running large-scale assays. Furthermore, we demonstrate stable clonal expansion of single mammalian, yeast, and bacterial cells; growth-based selections of >10,000 colonies; enhanced signal-to-noise in secretion assays; and high-purity selection of antibody-secreting cells based on activation of co-encapsulated T cell reporters (>30-fold signal, up to 100% selection purity). By combining the simplicity of a well plate with the functional precision of droplet microfluidics without requiring oil or custom instrumentation, capped nanovials realize accessible, high-throughput, and high-resolution experimentation.

journal_articles.title: Metazoan diversification characterized by elevated rates of evolution during the middle Ediacaran to earliest Cambrian.
journal_articles.abstract: To test causal hypotheses for the emergence of animal body plans, we analyze rates of molecular and phenotypic evolution across Opisthokonta, focusing on divergences within the Tonian-Ordovician interval. Both molecular and phenotypic rates increase through the Ediacaran, peaking in an Ediacaran and earliest Cambrian interval before declining thereafter. Partitioning phenotypic characters into categories relating to development, feeding, fossilization potential, locomotion, and nervous systems reveals distinct temporal patterns, with developmental traits contributing disproportionately to elevated rates in the metazoan stem lineage. Rate patterns show a temporal lag between the ecological changes integral to hypotheses of developmental evolution and the Cambrian agronomic, substrate, and information revolutions and earlier peaks in the evolution of the associated phenotypic characters. These patterns are largely independent of the timescale used. Overall, our results indicate that the primary phase of elevated evolutionary novelty occurred during the Ediacaran and culminated in the late Ediacaran-earliest Cambrian, providing the foundation for later ecological and taxonomic innovation.

journal_articles.title: N6-methyladenosine-dependent ARv7 translation couples lactate metabolism with enzalutamide resistance in prostate cancer.
journal_articles.abstract: Enzalutamide (Enz)-resistant prostate cancer (PCa) is a lethal disease that affects a broad population of elderly men. Experimental and clinical evidence has demonstrated that androgen receptor variant 7 (ARv7) plays a critical role in Enz-resistant (EnzR) PCa by functioning as a constitutively active transcription factor driving disease progression. However, the predictive value of the ARv7 transcript has not been fully recognized due to its low frequency in castration-resistant PCa. In this study, we identified ARv7 mRNA as an N6-methyladenosine (m6A)-modified transcript. Enz treatment increases METTL3-dependent m6A methylation of ARv7 mRNA at the A1177 site, which is subsequently recognized by the reader protein YTHDC2, leading to enhanced translation efficiency of ARv7. Furthermore, EnzR PCa exhibited elevated lactate metabolism, which regulated AR transcription through promoter-mediated epigenetic modifications at H3K9 and H3K14. Reactivated AR exhibited enhanced phase separation to transcriptionally up-regulate YTHDC2 expression. In vivo experiments demonstrated that targeting the METTL3-YTHDC2-ARv7 axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy to suppress EnzR PCa progression. Moreover, the METTL3 inhibitor STM2457 synergized with Enz to inhibit tumor growth without observable toxicity. Collectively, our findings suggest that the clinical utility of ARv7 may need to be reconsidered in light of its m6A-dependent translational regulation.

journal_articles.title: Pancreatic α cells function as MHC class II-dependent antigen-presenting cells in type 1 diabetes.
journal_articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an autoimmune disease characterized by T cell-mediated destruction of pancreatic β cells, in which antigen presentation is essential. Although professional antigen-presenting cells initiate autoreactive T cell responses, whether endocrine cells contribute to antigen presentation within inflamed islets remains unclear. Here, we show that pancreatic α cells acquire major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II (MHC-II)-dependent antigen-presenting capacity during T1D progression. Reanalysis of single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from nonobese diabetic (NOD) mice and human T1D islets revealed progressive up-regulation of MHC-II associated genes in α cells. Immunostaining validated the increased of MHC-II level both in NOD mice and patients with T1D. Mechanistically, inflammatory cytokines activated the Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT) pathway in α cells, leading to JAK-STAT-dependent MHC-II induction. Functionally, activated α cells internalized, processed, and presented exogenous antigens, acquired expression of costimulatory molecules, and promoted antigen-specific CD4+ T cell activation. These findings identify pancreatic α cells as nonprofessional antigen-presenting cells and expand the current understanding of antigen presentation in autoimmune diabetes.

journal_articles.title: Rapid, voxel-based 3D printing with yield-stress fluid inks.
journal_articles.abstract: Despite decades of progress, 3D printing still presents trade-offs in what materials can be printed and at what resolutions, speeds, and part volumes. We introduce direct ink additive lithography, or DIAL, to alleviate these trade-offs when printing with yield-stress, complex fluid inks used to print functional materials. DIAL combines translational photopatterning with ink sheet deposition for rapid, voxel-based 3D printing. Using model DIAL inks with kilopascal-scale yield stresses, we evaluate how ink rheology influences printing and compare DIAL against digital light processing (DLP) and direct ink writing (DIW). Since DIAL enables fast, high-throughput, support-free, and large-area printing, we showcase its broad potential for producing functional materials by printing multiscale architected, multimaterial, structural electrolyte, and hydrogel structures that are difficult if not impossible to 3D print today.

preprints.title: Where single-cell foundation models help: a benchmark of annotation, perturbation and regulatory inference against simple baselines
preprints.abstract: Single-cell foundation models (FMs) are proposed as general tools for cell-type annotation, in silico perturbation and gene-regulatory-network (GRN) inference. To identify where they add value, we benchmarked five FMs (scGPT, Geneformer V1 and V2, Nicheformer, scFoundation), CellOracle, supervised perturbation models including STATE, and task-matched simple baselines on the same data, from K562 Perturb-seq screens and primary cells to healthy-donor and isogenic leukodystrophy brain organoids, a public organoid CRISPR screen and lung cancer biopsies. FMs were most useful when labels had to be transferred across species: from human to mouse lung, Nicheformer reached 0.98 accuracy and Geneformer V2 and scFoundation about 0.90, against 0.68 for the best baseline. Zero-shot in silico perturbations captured the direction of real responses in K562, with up to 75% of perturbations shifted in the expected direction (scFoundation, p < 1e-8), and Geneformer V2 networks recovered patient-level tumour differential expression better than co-expression (fold enrichment 2.9 versus 2.0). Within a species, FM embeddings annotated cells as accurately as principal components. In organoids, predicted knockout effects were largely explained by where the target is expressed, and an expression-matched control test isolated the gene-specific part, 12 to 35% of the effects. Isogenic Canavan and Krabbe organoids and 4H patient organoids, with one library per line and time point, did not yet separate methods from differences between clones and donors, which defines the replication needed for future validation. Fine-tuning changed classification accuracy but not knockout rankings. We release the benchmark, baselines, pipeline checks and the isogenic reference task as the fmaudit package, so that new models can be evaluated on the tasks where FMs already help.
