preprints.title: ChAI-Net learns a regulatory code for chromatin co-accessibility
preprints.abstract: The regulation of chromatin accessibility is critical for cell function and identity. Advances in single-molecule long-read footprinting have enabled near-nucleotide-resolution readout of chromatin fiber organization, capturing both coordination of transcription factor (TF) binding and variation in nucleosome positioning previously obscured by bulk methods. Here we combine this technique with deep learning to study how protein-DNA interactions are coordinated within different types of cis-regulatory elements in mouse embryonic stem cells. First, we quantify the frequency with which pairs of positions are simultaneously accessible on individual molecules. Then, we train ChAI-Net, a neural network that predicts these locus-specific chromatin co-accessibility maps from the underlying DNA sequence. Through model interpretation and in silico experiments, we show that ChAI-Net learns unique combinations of sequence motifs underlying co-accessibility within enhancers, promoters, and CTCF-bound sites. Many of these motifs are missed when modeling average accessibility, suggesting a specific role in coordinated binding. ChAI-Net's regulatory grammar also highlights the importance of TF motif orientation, spacing, positioning, and co-occurrence in driving co-accessibility. Thus, our framework for extracting regulatory rules from footprinting data expands understanding of TF cooperativity, while laying the groundwork to elucidate how these rules vary across cellular contexts as single-molecule genomics is deployed at scale.

last_author.name: Pollard, K. S.

preprints.title: Single-cell transcriptomics of enriched rare neural lineages of Tribolium castaneum
preprints.abstract: Background Single-cell transcriptomic atlases have transformed our understanding of cell diversity. However, studies designed to profile entire tissues or organisms often omit or underrepresent rare cell populations. Enriching selected populations before sequencing offers a powerful approach to overcoming this limitation, but its application in insects has largely focused on Drosophila, limiting opportunities for comparative studies. Here, we establish complementary workflows for targeted transcriptomic profiling of rare neural populations in the red flour beetle, Tribolium castaneum. Results We developed two workflows combining population enrichment with single-cell or single-nucleus RNA sequencing. First, we generated cell suspensions from a transgenic reporter line labelling embryonic neuroblasts, enriched fluorescently labelled cells by fluorescence-activated cell sorting, and performed single-cell RNA sequencing. Second, we immunolabelled first-instar larval brains with an antibody against the nuclear transcription factor Rx, isolated and sorted labelled nuclei, and performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Both workflows yielded material suitable for transcriptomic profiling, demonstrating complementary reporter-based and antibody-based strategies for accessing selected neural populations at different developmental stages. Conclusions These workflows establish a methodological framework for targeted single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic studies of rare or specific neural populations in Tribolium. They provide practical starting points for adaptation to other insect systems, expanding opportunities for comparative investigations of neural development and cell-type evolution.

preprints.title: A Unique Promoter Architecture Defines Menin-KMT2A Complex Selectivity
preprints.abstract: Selective occupancy of chromatin-regulatory complexes is central to developmental gene regulation, yet the sequence determinants of this selectivity remain poorly understood. Using interpretable machine learning, we identify a composite promoter architecture comprising CpG islands flanked by several-kilobase A/T-rich domains (AT-flanks) that denotes high occupancy of the Menin-KMT2A histone-modifying complex at developmental and leukemia-associated genes. Genetic deletion and chromatin-contact analyses show that AT-flanks support KMT2A retention at linked CpG islands. We identify LEDGF as an A/T-rich DNA-associated protein required for Menin engagement at AT-flanks and sustained KMT2A promoter occupancy. AT-flank extent is associated with differential KMT2A loss following pharmacologic disruption of the Menin-KMT2A interaction, providing a genomic basis for heterogeneous target sensitivity to recently approved Menin inhibitors in acute leukemia. Beyond Menin-KMT2A, the same architecture distinguishes promoters with high canonical PRC1 occupancy across diverse cell types, revealing a shared sequence organization associated with distinct chromatin-regulatory states.

preprints.title: A single-cell multimodal foundation model enables cross modality analysis between transcriptome and chromatin
preprints.abstract: Most single-cell studies measure either gene expression or chromatin accessibility, and connecting the two usually requires fitting a model to each study. Here we present MUTUAL (MUltiome Transfer in a Unified Aligned Latent space), which keeps the single-cell foundation models scFoundation and EpiAgent frozen, combines their embeddings with linear summaries of each modality and learns a shared RNA--ATAC space from 3.0 million paired cells of 400 public multiome datasets. Applied without refitting to ten datasets not used for training, MUTUAL matched cells' RNA and ATAC profiles more accurately than methods fitted on other donors of the same dataset, annotated ATAC-only cells more accurately and transferred transcription-factor motif activity to RNA-only cells beyond what cell-type assignment provides. In a maturation series of stem-cell-derived islets, motif activity predicted from RNA largely reproduced the measured stage-wise changes when other libraries of the series served as the reference. MUTUAL makes public multiome data directly usable by single-modality studies.

preprints.title: FateDriver: Weakly supervised dual-view graph learning for transition-specific prioritization of candidate regulators in cellular reprogramming
preprints.abstract: Cellular reprogramming supports regenerative medicine, yet the endogenous regulators of a specified source-to-target transition remain incompletely defined. Existing computational methods rank candidate regulators from network topology, trajectory dynamics, or cell-state labels, leaving unused the factors experimentally delivered to induce the transition. We present FateDriver, a weakly supervised dual-view graph neural network that jointly represents cells and genes from single-cell transcriptomes, treats the delivered factors as sparse gene-level labels, and ranks the remaining genes for a specified transition under a positive--unlabeled formulation. Across two OSKM datasets and one GMT dataset, FateDriver ranked first or second among six methods in recovering externally curated reference genes, exceeded a supervision-matched non-graph model despite weaker co-expression with the delivered factors, and achieved the highest recovery of protein targets of pluripotency-inducing chemical cocktails in both OSKM datasets. Holding either the source or the endpoint fixed yielded distinct candidate programs, including a DDX58--interferon axis associated with cells lacking endogenous pluripotency markers. Applying the same framework to candidate source--target pairs prioritized distinct candidate origins for two in vivo partially reprogrammed intestinal populations. FateDriver converts sparse experimental knowledge into transition-specific hypotheses for regulator prioritization from single-cell trajectories.

preprints.title: Integrated transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of human cartilage reveals coordinated changes in fibronectin expression, splicing, and receptor signaling during osteoarthritis progression
preprints.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is defined by progressive loss of articular cartilage, but how chondrocytes change as the disease advances is unclear because most studies have focused on end-stage tissue. We profiled human knee articular cartilage across the full range of macroscopic OA grade, from young healthy to aged severe OA donors, by bulk RNA sequencing of 92 knees, single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 108,600 chondrocyte nuclei from 30 donors and single-nucleus multiome sequencing of 24 of these donors, treating grade as a continuous variable. With increasing grade, cartilage increased extracellular matrix (ECM) synthesis and remodeling genes, lost glucocorticoid-responsive, lipid-metabolic and antioxidant programs, and changed the splicing of a small set of ECM transcripts, led by the extra domain B (EDB) exon of fibronectin (FN1). Nine chondrocyte clusters were present in every disease stage and formed a continuum ordered by cartilage zone and hypertrophic differentiation, with PRG4+ superficial and COL10A1+ hypertrophic chondrocytes as the only distinct cell types at its ends and a pre-hypertrophic state between them. With grade, all clusters shared a response in which ECM production rose and homeostatic programs fell, and they differed in which of its components was strongest: ECM production in the superficial cells, the secretory pathway in the hypertrophic and CYTL1+ cells, and inflammatory signaling in the ANXA1+ and CRISPLD2+ cells. Inferred communication between chondrocytes was remodeled with stage. FN1 was induced in every cluster in excess of its fibril-assembly machinery, together with the fibronectin-cleaving protease HTRA1, and FN1 signaling shifted in receptor use from integrin 5{beta}1 toward CD44 and, less robustly, v{beta}8, accompanied by a rise in TGF-{beta}/SMAD response genes. In four early-OA donors, tenascin-C was already largely induced and the FN1 receptor shift from 5{beta}1 toward CD44 was partly present, whereas the rise of FN1 outside superficial chondrocytes, of FGF1 and of developmental and ossification programs came with progression. Chromatin accessibility changed in the same direction across clusters, with regions linked to FN1 opening and regions linked to ITGA5 closing. OA progression in human cartilage therefore appears to be a change of chondrocyte state that differs in emphasis along a zonal and hypertrophic continuum and includes changes in fibronectin regulation, production, processing, and receptor engagement.

preprints.title: Molecular dissection of the ChAHP complex subunits Adnp and Chd4 reveals common and divergent functions in retinal development
preprints.abstract: Epigenetic remodelling is thought to regulate the progression of competence states in neural progenitor cells. Here, we examined the functions of the ChAHP chromatin remodelling complex during retinal development. ChAHP consists of the ATP-dependent nucleosome remodeller CHD4, the zinc finger and homeodomain transcription factor ADNP, and the HP1 heterochromatin proteins (Cbx1/3/5). Notably, both CHD4 and ADNP are genetically associated with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), but ChAHP functions in neural development are not fully understood. In the retina, we found that both ADNP and CHD4 proteins were co-expressed ubiquitously in each cell type throughout development, and the two proteins formed a complex in vivo. Next, we generated retina-specific conditional knockouts (cKOs) to both Adnp and Chd4 using the Chx10-Cre driver. We observed phenotypic correspondence and divergence. Developmentally, we observed elevated cell death in both Adnp and Chd4 cKOs, but Adnp cKOs also exhibited deficits in progenitor numbers and proliferation. As a result, mature Adnp cKOs were hypoplastic with reductions in each cell type. We previously described a more complex phenotype in Chd4 cKOs, where cell fates were imbalanced and progenitor proliferation was prolonged, but these features were absent from the Adnp cKO. To understand how ChAHP regulates gene expression, we compared Adnp and Chd4 cKOs via scRNA-seq, which revealed common transcriptional signatures. However, Chd4 cKOs exhibited more severe effects on gene expression in line with its stronger effects on cell fate. We then performed cut&run-seq, which suggested that Adnp and Chd4 are recruited to the same genomic loci - many of which are also occupied by the Ctcf transcription factor. Taken together, our data suggest that ChAHP regulates retinal growth, but that CHD4 has additional ChAHP-independent functions in regulating progenitor fate decisions. These findings point to the idea that during neurogenesis, some brain regions may have greater dependence on ChAHP, and therefore greater vulnerability to genetic mutation.

preprints.title: Structural Evolution of Neural Networks during Zebrafish Early Development
preprints.abstract: The spatial architecture of neural networks underpins nervous system function, yet dynamic in vivo evidence for their early establishment process remains scarce. Here, using long-term confocal live-cell imaging of transgenic zebrafish, we dissected neural network development across the brain, yolk sac, and spinal cord at single-cell resolution. We reveal that repeated growth cone bifurcation is the fundamental cellular mechanism for network node formation. Despite distinct developmental origins, networks in all three regions exhibit highly conserved dynamics, strictly following Strahler hierarchical ordering and Hack's power-law scaling. Quantitative topological analysis shows that as development progresses, node numbers and clustering coefficients increase, while network density decreases. This reflects a structural optimization strategy balancing high functional efficiency with low wiring cost. These findings suggest that physical and geometric constraints, combined with simple local rules, drive the self-organization of complex neural networks, offering valuable principles for artificial network design.

preprints.title: scSTEC: Annotating Chromatin Subcompartments from Individual Single-Cell Hi-C Data via Direct Two-Dimensional Embedding and Chromosome-wise Consensus
preprints.abstract: \textbf{Motivation: }Single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) technologies enable the study of three-dimensional (3D) genome organization at individual-cell resolution. Many computational methods have been developed to infer hierarchical structures from scHi-C data. However, annotating chromatin subcompartments from sparse scHi-C data remains a challenge. The recently developed scGHOST provides a framework for single-cell subcompartment annotation, but relies on a deep learning-based architecture, a multi-step upstream pipeline involving cell embedding and matrix imputation, and cross-cell information sharing. These features complicate algorithmic interpretation and make the annotation of an individual cell dependent on information from other cells in the dataset. Hence, methods are needed that annotate subcompartments directly from an individual cell's own contact matrix, without complex upstream processing or cross-cell information sharing. \textbf{Results: }We developed scSTEC, a computational framework that annotates subcompartments directly from an individual scHi-C matrix without data imputation, complex upstream processing, or cross-cell data sharing. We show that the estimated inter-chromosomal matrix constructed by scGHOST is intrinsically of rank 2, revealing that the geometry relevant to clustering can be represented in two dimensions. Leveraging this low-dimensional structure, scSTEC performs direct subcompartment annotation through 2D genomic embedding and chromosome-wise consensus. Across bulk Hi-C, downsampled simulations, and real scHi-C datasets (four human cell lines, adult mouse cortex, developing mouse embryos, and developing olfactory sensory neurons), scSTEC achieves subcompartment annotations comparable to scGHOST despite operating on each cell independently, while providing greater algorithmic interpretability. Furthermore, subcompartments identified by scSTEC effectively resolve cell types, capture developmental dynamics, and show consistent associations with gene expression and epigenetic profiles. \\textbf{Availability: }scSTEC is freely available at \url{https://github.com/Ge-lab-pku/scSTEC}.

preprints.title: A subtype-specific gene regulatory program controls differential circuit integration of deep CA3 pyramidal neurons
preprints.abstract: How closely related neuronal subtypes integrate into different circuits remains poorly understood. Deep and superficial hippocampal CA3 pyramidal neurons (PNs) differ in intrinsic firing and mossy fiber (MF) input at specialized postsynaptic structures termed thorny excrescences (TEs). Combining developmental single-nucleus multiomics with genetic targeting, morphological analysis and electrophysiology, we identify the transcription factor ST18 as a regulator of deep CA3 subtype identity. ST18 marks sparsely thorny and burst-firing neurons, and gene regulatory analyses predict that it represses a superficial-associated program involved in dendritic spine development, synaptic organization, and electrophysiological properties. Postnatal ST18 loss shifts the transcriptional and chromatin landscape of deep CA3 PNs toward a superficial-like state. These molecular changes are accompanied by increased TE elaboration approaching superficial levels, enhanced excitatory synaptic activity, and reduced burst-firing. Together, these findings identify ST18-dependent restriction of an alternative subtype program as a mechanism linking molecular identity to distinct input connectivity patterns and intrinsic firing properties during postnatal circuit maturation.

preprints.title: Gene regulatory logic underlying the differentiation of mixed lineages in human thymic epithelial cells
preprints.abstract: The thymus enacts central tolerance through thymic (TECs), which present self-antigens to developing T cells self-reactive cells, preventing autoimmunity. Human TECs include populations that express lineage-committed programs corresponding to distinct peripheral tissues, yet how they acquire these programs and whether these TEC subpopulations are genetically related and conserved in mice remain unknown. Using matched single-cell gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility profiling of 126,687 human TECs, we identified 17 TEC subsets defined by their distinct expression profiles of 1,843 cell type restricted-antigens (CRAs) from 48 peripheral cell types. With a new phylogenetic reconstruction method, we show that lineage-committed TECs share a common ancestor, retain a thymus-specific mixed identity through co-expression of multiple CRA signatures, and are specified by coordinated activator and repressor regulons. We also identified a basement-membrane-collagen-rich state (BMC-TECs) with progenitor-like properties. Finally, mouse TECs shared the regulatory strategy but conserved few master transcription-factor drivers. This study mechanistically characterizes human TEC subpopulations and reveals the gene regulatory logic that leads to their distinct diversification and mixed identities in humans and mice.

preprints.title: Inflammation reshapes epidermal and leukocyte differentiation resulting in altered glucocorticoid responsiveness
preprints.abstract: Glucocorticoids are widely prescribed anti-inflammatory drugs that act on nearly all cell types due to the ubiquitous expression of the glucocorticoid receptor (GR). While the molecular mechanisms of GR activation have been studied extensively, it is less well understood how GR signaling modulates cell type-specific responses during inflammation. Using the unique attributes of the zebrafish, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize GR-mediated transcriptional regulation under conditions of wounding-induced inflammation. We found specific cell populations that occurred only under inflammatory conditions within epidermal cells, macrophages and neutrophils. The inflammation-specific subset of epidermal cells showed elevated expression of inflammatory markers, and these cells exhibited a reduced transactivation response to dexamethasone. This reduction in GR activation was also observed in the inflammation-specific subset of macrophages, but not in neutrophils, which retained dexamethasone responsiveness. By correlating the dexamethasone responsiveness with transcriptional coregulator expression, we identified candidate regulatory mechanisms underlying differential GR responsiveness across cell types. Taken together, we provided unique mechanistic insights into cell differentiation during a local inflammatory response and cell type-specific glucocorticoid responsiveness in vivo.

preprints.title: Perturbation-induced gene programs map the hidden regulatory architecture of complex diseases
preprints.abstract: Steady-state molecular profiles incompletely capture the regulatory programs through which genetic variation influences complex disease, particularly programs that emerge only when cells are perturbed. Here, we introduce Perturbscape, a computational framework that learns multiscale gene programs for individual perturbations in a CRISPR Perturb-seq screen using linear and nonlinear contrastive approaches alongside complementary program-learning methods, and integrates them with human genetics to prioritize disease-relevant genes, perturbations and downstream regulatory pathways. Across 15,859 perturbation-by-context profiles from 7 Perturb-seq systems and 53 complex diseases and traits (mean GWAS N=291K), perturbation-induced programs showed up to 4.3-fold higher heritability informativeness than analogous steady-state multi-tissue gene prioritization, and retained significant conditional heritability informativeness across all 34 matched cell system-trait comparisons after accounting for steady-state prioritization. Preserving perturbation-specific programs further yielded 2.5-5.3-fold higher trait relevance scores than programs derived from control cells, pooled perturbations or differential-expression summaries. In K562, Perturbscape-prioritized genes showed stronger enrichment for rare-variant burden genes than steady-state prioritization and were supported by orthogonal enhancer CRISPRi screens. In HepG2, LDL cholesterol-associated perturbation-induced programs specifically revealed statin-responsive pathways not significantly enriched by steady-state PoPS prioritization, supported by pharmacological transcriptional responses and population plasma proteomics. Perturbscape also recovered blood-related trait-conditioned trans-regulatory relationships that were specifically supported by population trans-eQTLs in IFN-gamma-stimulated monocytes (OR = 1.30, P=1.6e-05). Perturbscape further revealed developmental-stage-specific convergence between monogenic diabetes regulators and polygenic T2D risk during pancreatic islet differentiation, and neuronal-subclass-specific autism-associated regulatory programs in vivo. Together, these findings establish perturbation-induced gene programs as a complementary layer of disease-relevant regulatory information, revealing genetically informative pathways and context-specific regulatory relationships incompletely represented by steady-state molecular atlases.

preprints.title: Single-cell foundation models transfer across deep evolutionary distances
preprints.abstract: Single-cell foundation models are trained mostly on human and other vertebrate cells, yet are proposed as general-purpose models. Whether they transfer far beyond their training species is unknown. We evaluated zero-shot embeddings from Geneformer, scGPT and UCE against PCA and scVI in developmental atlases of Dictyostelium discoideum and Caenorhabditis elegans, separated from humans by 1.2 billion and 600 million years. Without retraining, the models recovered developmental order and preserved organism-specific cell identities. UCE encodes genes by protein sequence and could use 97% of measured genes, whereas Geneformer and scGPT, after ortholog mapping, used under one-fifth. UCE performed most consistently, often exceeding species-native baselines. Restricted to ortholog-mappable genes, it still scored above vocabulary-based models on five of six annotation tasks, some narrowly. Foundation models can thus yield informative cell embeddings across more than a billion years of evolution, and protein-sequence gene representations make these embeddings more complete and often more accurate.

preprints.title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS
preprints.abstract: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

preprints.title: VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq
preprints.abstract: Summary: Gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq is challenging because genomic regions informative of cell identity can vary across genes and tissues, while broadly accessible regions may provide limited cell-type-discriminative information. We developed VIGAT, a vision-language model (VLM)-guided tool that automates visual interpretation of ATAC coverage plots for adaptive gene activity quantification. VIGAT jointly examines accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes, integrating genomic annotations and biological context to select gene-specific regions enriched for cluster-discriminative signals. Selected regions are used to generate a gene-by-cell activity matrix. Across 196 paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets, VIGAT outperformed five existing methods in recovering marker-associated accessibility enriched in the corresponding cell populations, demonstrating the utility of VLM-guided visual reasoning for scalable gene activity quantification. Availability and implementation: VIGAT is implemented as an open-source R package and is freely available at https://github.com/beijie02/VIGAT.

last_author.name: Ji, Z.
last_author.affiliation: Duke University School of Medicine

preprints.title: Dissecting functional elements in giant genomes using the first generation of high quality salamander assemblies
preprints.abstract: Salamanders are an enduring and historically significant group that helped originate multiple scientific fields of study, including regeneration, cytogenetics, experimental embryology, cloning, evolutionary developmental biology and evolution of extreme genome size. We generated a high-quality, single haplotype assembly for the 32 Gb axolotl (Ambystoma mexicanum) genome using an F1 hybrid between axolotl and a divergent relative the tiger salamander (A. tigrinum). Using multi-genome alignments to other salamanders that meet VGP metrics, we leveraged strong conservation of karyotypic structure to identify >523,000 highly conserved non-coding elements within massively expanded intronic and intergenic regions, the vast majority of which are unique to the salamander lineage. Orthogonal measures of chromatin state and enhancer activity confirmed that many conserved elements correspond to cis-regulatory sequences and identified several thousand that are utilized during regeneration. The conserved elements identified here will enable robust functional genomic analyses of tissue regeneration and other traits that uniquely empower salamander models in biological research.

last_author.name: Smith, J. J.
last_author.affiliation: University of Kentucky

preprints.title: Synthetic MPRA perturbation supervision improves variant-effect prediction in sequence-to-function models
preprints.abstract: Deep learning sequence-to-function (S2F) models learn to predict functional readouts, such as gene expression, from genetic sequence. However, these models are trained predominantly on the reference genome and struggle to accurately predict the effect of genetic variation on gene expression. Massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) explore the direct impact of genetic variation on gene expression, but saturation-mutagenesis MPRAs that measure variant effects directly remain limited, thereby restricting their use for fine-tuning S2F models. In this work, we investigate fine-tuning Borzoi, a state-of-the-art S2F model, on model-generated synthetic MPRA variant-effect data as a scalable alternative to overcome limits on the availability of supervised training data for genetic variation. First, we trained an ensemble of 16 models on 110,359 K562 MPRA measurements. Then, we distilled their predictions into a single student model using MPRA elements associated with 1,000 genes. The distilled model was subsequently used to generate synthetic variant-effect labels across increasing numbers of genes (50 to 1,000), with 600 variants per gene, to fine-tune Borzoi. Performance improved as we included more genes in training. In data-limited settings, training on more genes with fewer variants per gene performed better than training on fewer genes with more variants per gene, given the same number of total variants. Compared to pre-trained Borzoi, Borzoi fine-tuned on 600,000 synthetic samples across 1,000 genes increased Pearson correlation from 0.28 to 0.54 on CAGI5 promoter variants and from 0.39 to 0.46 on 903 GTEx fine-mapped whole-blood expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs). Importantly, these improvements were achieved while preserving the pre-trained performance across all 7,611 output tracks. Furthermore, fine-tuned Borzoi recovered regulatory motifs identified by the MPRA model in genes unseen during training, suggesting that learned regulatory features can generalize across loci. Together, these results provide a proof of concept that model-generated synthetic supervision can improve variant effect prediction in S2F models while preserving their original pre-trained capabilities, offering a scalable strategy toward capturing the impact of genetic variation on gene regulation.

last_author.name: Battle, A.
last_author.affiliation: Johns Hopkins University

preprints.title: Genome-wide chromatin accessibility during early embryogenesis in a generalist cichlid fish
preprints.abstract: Background Lake Malawi's haplochromine cichlids are one of the most rapid and species-rich vertebrate adaptive radiations known, generating hundreds of species within < 1 million years, yet how regulatory regions shape their embryonic development remains poorly understood. Astatotilapia calliptera, a generalist riverine lineage and proxy for the ancestral stock that seeded this radiation, offers a developmental chromatin baseline against which regulatory divergence in specialised lineages can be compared. Results We generated genome-wide ATAC-seq profiles of A. calliptera embryos across three developmental stages (3, 7 and 12 days post-fertilisation, dpf), identifying 550,876-701,889 accessible chromatin peaks per stage. Accessible chromatin was enriched at gene promoters and at both highly conserved and accelerated conserved noncoding elements at every stage. The functional repertoire of accessible-promoter genes shifted across development, from early patterning at 3 dpf to the broadest regulatory repertoire at 7 dpf, and an increasingly neural- and locomotory-behaviour-enriched repertoire by 12 dpf, coinciding with post-hatching motor maturation. Differential accessibility showed that chromatin opening, rather than closing, dominates the earliest transitions (3 vs 7 and 3 vs 12 dpf), driven mostly by general metabolic genes, whereas the smaller, later 7 vs 12 dpf transition combined targeted gains at tissue-remodelling and apoptosis genes with losses at genes governing early neural and retinal patterning; almost all of these losses (96%) were at promoters that had opened between 3 and 7 dpf, indicating transient rather than sustained opening. Transcription factor (TF) footprinting identified stage-specific regulatory activity among developmentally important TFs, while the broader TF-promoter network remained topologically stable across all three stages, built around conserved hub regulators of core neural and sensory patterning genes e.g., SOX2, FOXG1, PTF1A, SOX10. This suggests that wiring is established early and largely maintained, following the hourglass model, with developmental progression driven by changes in activity of this conserved programme. Conclusions Together, these findings establish the first embryonic epigenomic resource for A. calliptera, revealing a developmental chromatin landscape of broad early opening and progressive functional specialisation, and providing a comparative framework for understanding how regulatory evolution has shaped Lake Malawi cichlid diversification.

last_author.name: Mehta, T. K.
last_author.affiliation: University of Liverpool

preprints.title: HOX13 factors shape cell developmental transcriptional program through multiple mechanisms that regulate chromatin accessibility.
preprints.abstract: HOX transcription factors pattern embryonic tissues and organs and have post-developmental roles in adult tissue maintenance and function. They can bind inaccessible chromatin, but their roles in chromatin accessibility remain unclear. Using in vivo and in vitro approaches, we show that HOX13 factors promote both initial opening and maintenance of accessibility at subsets of target regulatory elements. Mechanistically, the HOX13-dependent chromatin accessibility involves both its homodimerization and the recruitment of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex. Our findings indicate that SWI/SNF contributes to the extent of opening but is neither sufficient nor the sole determinant of HOXA13 pioneering activity. In iPSCs, HOXA13 induction rapidly reduces pluripotency gene expression while activating an early osteochondrogenic transcriptional program, which, at least in part, corresponds to direct gene regulation by HOXA13. Together, these findings identify multiple, context-dependent contributions to HOX13-mediated chromatin regulation, resulting in early lineage-associated responses.

last_author.name: Kmita, M.

preprints.title: Predicting single-molecule chromatin distribution from DNA sequence
preprints.abstract: Genome regulation unfolds through dynamic and stochastic single-molecule events. Deep learning models that read gene regulatory activities from DNA sequences have markedly advanced our ability to predict cell-population-level averages. However, they cannot capture the full spectrum of heterogeneity and dynamics at the single-molecule level, which directly reflect the underlying mechanisms of genome regulation. Here, we introduce a sequence-to-distribution (S2d) framework that directly models the entire probabilistic distribution of single-molecule chromatin states from DNA sequence alone. We used this framework to train Mola, a model of single-molecule chromatin accessibility. We harness Mola to investigate sequence-based regulatory code and mechanisms for multiple aspects of chromatin regulation at the single-molecule level. By quantifying sequence-driven nucleosome regulation, we reveal distinct modes of transcription factor engagement with nucleosomes, including a novel nucleosome-trapping factor, ZNF146. We characterized the sequence determinants governing the +1 nucleosome after transcription start sites and identified YY1 as the strongest +1 nucleosome-positioning factor. Leveraging long-context single-molecule modeling, we further discovered a shared sequence basis for the co-accessibility of regulatory elements and the co-footprinting of transcription factors. Joint prediction of DNA methylation and accessibility reveals a sequence-driven bimodal state mediated by methylation-sensitive transcription factors. Beyond static single-molecule snapshots, the S2d framework can generate pseudo-dynamic trajectories of chromatin states and propose a roadmap toward genome-wide chromatin dynamics. Moreover, we showed that Mola can predict and interpret the effects of genetic variants at the single-molecule level, revealing how sequence changes reshape distal regulatory coordination. Together, this sequence-to-distribution framework lays the foundation for understanding how genomic sequence encodes stochastic and dynamic genome regulation, and how genetic variation changes it, one molecule at a time.

preprints.title: Variation in the embryonic cell lineages of Caenorhabditis elegans natural populations
preprints.abstract: Developmental variation has often been appreciated as a major phenotypic substrate of evolutionary innovation in multicellular organisms. Although quantification of developmental variation in isogenic populations has a long history, it has been difficult to accomplish across natural populations until recently. Given its invariant cell lineage, Caenorhabditis elegans represents an ideal model system for studying how natural diversity in development is expressed at the resolution of single cells, cell lineages, and the whole embryo. Using embGAN, a deep-learning pipeline that enables label-free lineage tracing without the bottleneck and potential confounding effects of generating transgenic strains, we reconstructed the early embryonic lineage of 78 embryos spanning eight genetic backgrounds, including six wild strains, and quantified cell-cycle timing with a lineage-aligned graph metric that separates global rescaling of developmental rate from localized changes in lineage structure. We found that cell-cycle timing differs reproducibly among genotypes, with between-strain variation consistently exceeding within-strain variation. The magnitude of this variation was itself genotype-specific and not correlated with levels of genetic divergence. Unlike the global shifts in the tempo of development that dominate divergence between species, these differences are predominantly in lineage patterning, changing the timing of specific divisions, and they align to cell fate. Thus, the invariant lineage of C. elegans is built on a structured, genotype-specific landscape of developmental variation, a potential source of trait variation from which drift in developmental systems can emerge.

preprints.title: flashscenic: Accelerated GRN Analysis with RegDiffusion for Large-Scale Single-Cell Data
preprints.abstract: Single-cell gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis via the SCENIC framework provides biologically interpretable cell-state representations through motif-validated transcription factor (TF) regulon activities. However, sequential, CPU-bound implementations (pySCENIC) constrain scalability to highly variable genes and make the repeated executions needed to resolve network stochasticity computationally prohibitive. Furthermore, while regulon activity is hypothesized to mitigate technical batch effects, its integration performance has never been quantitatively assessed against modern data integration benchmarks. We present flashscenic, an end-to-end GPU-accelerated framework that resolves these bottlenecks and expands the practical scope of single-cell regulatory genomics. By reformulating module construction, cisTarget motif pruning, and AUCell scoring into batched GPU tensor operations, flashscenic achieves a 12- to 27-fold downstream speedup over pySCENIC, while maintaining strict numerical equivalence (Pearson r = 0.9996). Leveraging this throughput, we conducted the first systematic benchmark of nine consensus aggregation strategies across multiple independent tissue cohorts, demonstrating that discrete post-pruning recurrence voting ([≥]50% recurrence, [≥]5 targets per regulon) maximizes biological fidelity. Finally, data integration benchmarking across a 116,043-cell acute myeloid leukemia (AML) atlas quantitatively demonstrates that uncorrected TF activity provides an intrinsic, unsupervised batch-integration benefit over raw PCA. Combining it with a standard batch integration method matches or outperforms canonical expression-based integration while accurately recovering lineage-defining and oncogenic regulators (CEBPA, HOXA9). flashscenic is available via pip install flashscenic, with source code and tutorials at https://github.com/haozhu233/flashscenic.

preprints.title: Apelin signaling controls neuroendocrine homeostasis via Atoh8-dependent transcriptional regulation
preprints.abstract: Apelin is a pleiotropic peptide hormone with established roles in cardiovascular function, angiogenesis, and metabolism, but its contribution to neuroendocrine development and function remains poorly understood. Here, using genetic loss-of-function and inducible gain-of-function approaches in zebrafish, we show that Apelin signaling is dosage-sensitive and required for normal development, reproductive capacity, and physiological homeostasis. Both apelin deficiency and apelin overexpression disrupted embryonic development and reduced adult lifespan, while exhibiting markedly reduced fertility in both sexes. Transcriptomic profiling revealed broad changes in neuroendocrine, hormonal, stress-response, and inflammatory genes with young adult mutant expression profiles resembling those of aged wild-type fish. Both loss and excess of Apelin also disrupted hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) axis development, reducing hypothalamic thyrotropin-releasing hormone-expressing cells, pituitary gonadotropic cell populations, and thyroid gland volume. Transcriptomic analyses identified atoh8, encoding a basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor, as a candidate effector of Apelin signaling. Apelin expression increased atoh8 expression during early embryogenesis, whereas atoh8 mRNA partially rescued developmental defects in apelin mutants, including hypothalamic and pituitary markers, and thyroid volume. Conversely, atoh8 crispants displayed thyroid and pituitary abnormalities, supporting a role for Atoh8 in neuroendocrine development. Together, these findings establish Apelin signaling as a dosage-sensitive regulator of zebrafish development and tissue homeostasis and identify Atoh8 as a functional downstream effector that partially mediates Apelin-dependent HPT axis formation. This work links peptide hormone signaling to neuroendocrine development and provides a framework for investigating its broader contributions to vertebrate physiology, reproduction and aging.

preprints.title: CloneVI: A deep generative model for deciphering the relationships between cell state and mitochondrial genotype
preprints.abstract: Cellular diversity arises from both genetic lineages and non-genetic regulation of cell states, and knowing which cell states are tied to lineages is central to understanding how clones shape disease. Single-cell multi-omics technologies measure mitochondrial DNA mutations together with gene expression or chromatin accessibility in the same cells, but clones are usually inferred from mutations alone, making such clones difficult to identify. We developed CloneVI, a deep generative model that infers clonal structure from a latent cell state derived from gene expression or chromatin accessibility. It estimates the clonal probability of each cell from this cell state, together with the allele frequency of each clone by reconstructing the observed mutation counts. In simulated data, CloneVI recovered the ground-truth clonal structure in both single-clone and mixed-clone cell populations. In clonal hematopoiesis single-cell RNA-seq data with enriched mitochondrial transcripts, the inferred clones were associated with specific mitochondrial DNA mutations, and some of them showed high expression of a T-cell receptor variable-region gene. In chronic lymphocytic leukemia mitochondrial single-cell ATAC-seq data, CloneVI separated populations with different heteroplasmy levels and identified increased PAX9 accessibility. In a multi-donor ovarian tumor cohort, CloneVI captured mutant-cell populations enriched in particular cell states, and a differential test weighted by the clonal probability revealed the transcription factor activity of the cell state in which the mutant cells concentrated. CloneVI thus identifies populations defined by mitochondrial DNA mutations and associated with cell states in single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data. CloneVI is available at https://github.com/TaichiHIBI/cloneVI.

preprints.title: Genome-wide loss of chromatin accessibility coexists with selectively elevated RNA abundance in nutrient-starved U2OS cells
preprints.abstract: Background Chromatin accessibility is widely used as a proxy for regulatory potential and is often interpreted together with RNA-seq to infer gene-regulatory responses. However, the quantitative relationship between chromatin accessibility and transcript abundance may become difficult to interpret, particularly under acute cellular stress. Metabolic challenges such as nutrient deprivation are known to induce extensive chromatin remodelling and transcriptional reprogramming, raising the question of whether changes in transcript abundance are directly governed by chromatin accessibility in these contexts. Clarifying this relationship is critical for interpreting epigenomic data under stress conditions, and requires careful distinction between Tn5 accessibility, relative steady-state RNA abundance and transcriptional output. Results We integrated ATAC-seq and RNA-seq analyses in human U2OS osteosarcoma cells following 18 h of severe nutrient deprivation. We found that starvation was associated with a genome-wide reduction in accessibility and almost all significantly altered accessible regions showed reduced signal relative to actively growing cells. This decrease affected promoter- and enhancer-associated regions alike, including housekeeping-gene promoters and CTCF-motif sites. In contrast, RNA-seq revealed a more selective change in relative steady-state RNA abundance: only a minority of expressed genes were differentially regulated, and approximately 64% of differentially expressed genes showed increased relative RNA abundance. Changes in accessibility and transcript abundance were modestly correlated at promoters (Pearson r = 0.25) and weakly at enhancers (r = 0.10), and together explained only ~6% of the variance in transcript abundance changes. The relationship was graded: genes with the smallest promoter losses were about four times as likely to show increased RNA abundance as genes with the largest losses, independently of baseline promoter accessibility. Within-condition analyses similarly showed only modest relationships between promoter accessibility and RNA abundance in both actively growing and starved cells. Pathway-level analysis of mRNA abundance revealed the expected repression of biosynthetic and growth-related programmes, including ribosome biogenesis, translation and cellular growth, together with a less anticipated relative activation of stress-adaptive programmes, including extracellular matrix organisation, lipid and cholesterol metabolism, small GTPase signalling and developmental processes. For genes within these activated programmes, increased steady-state mRNA abundance was observed despite reduced ATAC-seq accessibility at associated regulatory regions. Exon-intron analyses of RNA-seq data indicated that these changes predominantly reflect altered RNA production. Metabolic labelling of nascent RNA at selected loci confirmed increased transcription of genes involved in adaptive programmes despite reduced promoter and enhancer accessibility, alongside with reduced production of biosynthetic transcripts and rRNA. Conclusions These findings demonstrate that chromatin accessibility and steady-state RNA abundance are only modestly coupled during severe nutrient deprivation, against a baseline of similarly modest promoter accessibility-abundance coupling. This underscores the limited ability of ATAC-seq accessibility to predict transcript abundance under this stress condition and supports a model in which chromatin accessibility acts as a permissive rather than deterministic layer of gene regulation. The selective induction of adaptive programmes, confirmed here at the level of RNA production, shows that transcriptional activation can occur despite genome-wide loss of ATAC-seq accessibility. Because ATAC-seq reports Tn5 accessibility rather than physical chromatin compaction, we interpret compaction as a plausible mechanistic model compatible with the current observations, which will require direct orthogonal validation.

preprints.title: Mapping the regulatory wiring of endothelial cell differentiation reveals a critical role for Hippo mechanosignaling
preprints.abstract: At each step of development, stem cells encounter a branching decision to differentiate into one type of cell or another. This decision is executed through the action of competing gene programs that specify different cellular identities. Consequently, creating a comprehensive map of the gene programs that drive each branching step of human cell differentiation remains a long-sought goal of developmental and stem cell biology. Here, we introduce a framework combining genome-wide CRISPR screens, single-cell readouts, and gene program inference to systematically discover and characterize regulators of cell differentiation. This framework includes a method for CRISPR perturbations paired with single-cell RNA-seq called circular capture Perturb-seq (CC-Perturb-seq), which improves gRNA detection from split-pool combinatorial indexing protocols and enables perturbing many candidate regulators to map their effects on gene programs. We applied this framework to map how human pluripotent stem cells differentiate into arterial endothelial cells (ECs), and identified 174 regulators that promote or inhibit EC differentiation. By tracking gene programs across three stages of differentiation, we resolved when and how regulators divert cells toward alternative fates. This map revealed an unexpected requirement for the Hippo mechanosignaling pathway in EC specification. During lateral mesoderm differentiation, Hippo mechanosignaling was required to activate ETV2, the master transcriptional regulator of endothelial identity. Inhibiting Hippo blocked ETV2 even in the presence of VEGF and diverted progenitors to a mesenchymal fate in vitro. Likewise, Hippo signaling was required for maximal etv2 expression in developing zebrafish embryos. Conversely, pharmacologically activating the Hippo pathway increased the purity of both arterial and venous EC differentiation in vitro. Our framework thus identifies novel regulators of endothelial cell differentiation, improves stem-cell differentiation protocols via manipulation of mechanosignaling, and provides a generalizable platform for mapping the regulatory wiring of human development.

preprints.title: Single-nucleus multiome profiling reveals osteocyte-centered remodeling of human subchondral bone across osteoarthritis severity
preprints.abstract: Objective: Subchondral bone remodeling is a hallmark of osteoarthritis (OA), but osteocytes, the principal regulators of bone homeostasis, have been inaccessible to single-cell studies because they are embedded in mineralized matrix. We aimed to define the cellular, transcriptional and chromatin changes of human subchondral bone across OA severity, osteocytes included, and to identify candidate signals between cartilage and bone. Design: Subchondral bone from the medial femoral condyle of human knees graded by the Outerbridge system was analyzed by bulk RNA sequencing (89 knees) and by single-nucleus multiome sequencing of gene expression and chromatin accessibility after mechanical nuclear isolation (16 donors). Three hypotheses were prespecified: with increasing OA severity, (1) the osteoprogenitor fraction increases, (2) the osteocyte fraction increases, and (3) osteocyte SMAD2/3 motif activity increases. Results: With OA severity, bulk expression shifted toward extracellular matrix and ossification programs. The atlas resolved 26 cell states among 61,570 nuclei, including 906 osteocytes. Osteoprogenitors (p = 0.003) and osteocytes (p = 0.036) increased in share along an osteogenic continuum that starts from CXCL12-abundant reticular cells. Chondrocytes at the osteochondral junction upregulated FN1, FGF1, FGF2 and TNFSF11 without increased hypertrophic gene expression, and their share of the inferred FN1 signal received by osteocytes rose from 4% in normal knees to 33% in severe OA. Osteocyte SMAD2/3 motif activity increased with severity (rho = 0.70, p = 0.003), and all three hypotheses remained significant after Holm correction. Across the osteogenic lineage, SMAD2/3 activity correlated with junction chondrocyte FN1 (rho = 0.63, p = 0.017), and in osteocytes it was accompanied by TGF-{beta}-responsive matrix genes and perilacunar-remodeling genes. Conclusions: This osteocyte-inclusive atlas of human OA subchondral bone shows expansion of the osteogenic compartment and a rise of osteocyte SMAD2/3-linked matrix remodeling with disease, and identifies chondrocyte-derived FN1 as a candidate contributor to cartilage-bone communication associated with osteocyte TGF-{beta}/SMAD2/3 signaling.

preprints.title: ARCADE disentangles cell abundance from continuous transcriptional state in spatial transcriptomics
preprints.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics is widely used to infer both cell-type abundance and within-type transcriptional variation, but these signals are difficult to separate in mixed spot-level measurements. Here, we present ARCADE, a computational framework that addresses two major sources of uncertainty in spatial analysis: unstable single-cell references and entanglement between abundance and cell state. ARCADE first builds a robust reference through hyperparameter optimization and consensus filtering, then performs spatial inference in two stages by estimating cell-type composition before modeling continuous intratype transcriptional programs around this compositional anchor. Across simulated and semi-synthetic benchmarks, ARCADE improves deconvolution accuracy and yields more stable state inference than existing approaches. In matched human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex datasets with spatial proteogenomic readouts, ARCADE distinguishes localized cell enrichment from astrocyte and microglial activation programs. These results show that decoupled modeling can improve the interpretability of spatial transcriptomic signals in complex tissues.

preprints.title: Ambivalent roles of nonsense-mediated mRNA decay in heat stress tolerance
preprints.abstract: RNA homeostasis is essential for gene regulation and cellular survival; however, how RNA degradation pathways contribute to stress adaptation remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the role of the nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) in regulating heat stress (HS) memory in a long-term acquired thermotolerance assay. NMD-deficient Arabidopsis thaliana mutants upf1-5 and upf3-1 exhibited a biphasic phenotype: they displayed transiently elevated heat tolerance during early recovery but became more sensitive to heat during late recovery. Genetic analysis of upf3;hsfa2 and upf3;hsfa3 double mutants demonstrated that the early heat tolerance occurs independently of both HsfA2 and HsfA3 HS-memory transcription factors. Under non-treated conditions, the upf3-1 transcriptome exhibited baseline priming of heat-shock responsive transcripts, likely accounting for the initial heat tolerance. Further transcriptome profiling revealed that upf3-1 mutants exhibited reduced levels of the functional HsfA2 isoform (HsfA2-I) and attenuated expression of the HsfA2-dependent thermomemory regulon following the triggering stress. NMD deficiency also upregulated immune-response genes while repressing developmental and cell-wall-associated pathways. Together, impaired HsfA2-dependent thermomemory and a compromised growth defense balance underlies the late heat sensitivity of NMD deficient plants. Overall, NMD acts as a dual-action post-transcriptional regulator that coordinates the transition from stress response to growth resumption.

preprints.title: An invariant network architecture with broadly expressed regulators distinguishes cell-type from cell-state identity in situ
preprints.abstract: Core regulatory networks (CRNs) of tissue-specific master transcription factors (TFs) are essential for defining cell identity and are widely used to reprogram cells and to decipher pathogenic mechanisms. However, to date, CRNs have only been described at the cell-type level: their characteristics in the distinct states that a single cell type can adopt have not been examined. This leaves open what the cell-type CRNs actually represent. Here, using the zonated hepatocyte states of the mouse liver as a model system, we construct the first state-level CRNs in a native tissue. For this purpose, we developed a robust LCM-Spatial-ATAC-seq method that achieves bulk-level data quality from microdissected cell populations. By identifying what is shared among the state-level CRNs, we determined what is cell-type defining: an invariant sub-network of core-regulatory TFs (crTFs) that maintains identical positions and conserved interactions in the CRNs. Unexpectedly, the top positions of this invariant sub-network are occupied by broadly expressed TFs rather than the well-established master TFs, which reside downstream. Yet the state-level CRNs are clearly different, both in terms of composition and interactions. The former are dominated by zone-specific regulators, whereas the latter are spread throughout the network, encompassing about one third of all interactions between the states. Thus, our results reveal a novel dual character of a cell's CRN: an invariant sub-network that defines the cell-type identity, together with a variable peripheral network that underlies its state specialization.

preprints.title: Decoding Cell-type Specific Gene Regulation with CellReg3D by Integrating DNA Large Language Models and 3D Genome Structure
preprints.abstract: Gene regulation is a core biological mechanism crucial for organismal growth and development. Recent advances in deep learning, coupled with increasing computational resources, have enabled large-scale modelling of gene regulatory processes. While numerous models have been proposed, effectively capturing long-range genomic interactions remains a central challenge. Here, we introduce CellReg3D, a multiscale and multi-modal deep learning framework designed to model cell-type-specific gene regulation by integrating local sequence patterns with long-range genomic interactions. Existing approaches often overlook the contribution of 3D genome architecture and face limitations in combining sequence-based features with chromatin interaction data. Specifically, CellReg3D overcomes these gaps by leveraging a DNA language model to encode sequence-level information and incorporating Hi-C-derived 3D chromatin interactions to capture chromatin spatial organization. We demonstrate that CellReg3D effectively learns epigenetic patterns and chromatin activity states, achieving state-of-the-art performance in predicting epigenetic marks and gene expression profiles across multiple cell types. Using interpretable methods, we illustrate how the model identifies cell-type-specific regulatory mechanisms and prioritizes functional non-coding variants. Furthermore, we apply CellReg3D to enhance the interpretation of expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) and uncover novel potential gene regulatory interactions. Overall, CellReg3D offers a integrative framework for decoding regulatory genomics, unifying sequence and 3D genome structure data to advance variant prioritization, disease mechanism discovery, and personalized functional genomics.

preprints.title: Ferroptosis of selective progenitor cell types during embryogenesis ensures proper organ morphogenesis
preprints.abstract: Ferroptosis, a form of non-apoptotic cell death, is induced by lipid peroxidation resulting from an intracellular accumulation of labile iron (1). While apoptosis is involved in embryonic development (2), the role of ferroptosis in embryogenesis is unknown. Here, we report that the ferroptosis process occurs in the embryonic lung and kidney at mid- and late-gestation. In these tissues, pro-ferroptotic cells include subpopulations of the Sox9+ distal lung epithelial cells and the Flk1+ vascular progenitors in the kidney glomeruli. Lipidomic analysis reveals mixed lipid peroxidation as the driver for ferroptosis. The role of ferroptosis in the morphogenesis of these organs was confirmed by triple positivity of TfR1, 4-HNE and TUNEL, mitochondrial defects, cell membrane breakage, dead cell remnants, single-cell RNA-sequencing of a ferroptosis gene signature. Genetic manipulation of Gpx4, an endogenous inhibitor of ferroptosis. Further, genetic knockout or transgenic overexpression of Gpx4 affects lung and kidney development and results in cystic lungs and kidneys. Notably, conditional deletion Gpx4 results in hypoplasia of the lung epithelia and of the renal glomeruli, while transgenic overexpression of Gpx4 resulted in atelectasis with collapsed lung alveoli and hypertrophic glomeruli. Together, these findings show that ferroptosis regulates lung and kidney morphogenesis by acting in key progenitor cell populations during gestation. Supplementation of iron or polyunsaturated fatty acid during pregnancy has implications for organogenesis.

preprints.title: GSET: Gene Signals from Embedding Trajectories select compact contexts for mechanistic GRN inference
preprints.abstract: Mechanistic inference of gene regulatory networks from temporal transcriptomic data can become computationally prohibitive at transcriptome scale, making gene selection an important determinant of which regulatory relationships can be recovered. However, gene selection for GRN inference commonly relies on static expression or co-expression structure, rather than prioritizing dynamically informative genes whose temporal patterns capture how transcriptional programs change and relate to one another. We introduce GSET (Gene Signals from Embedding Trajectories), an upstream retrieval framework that extracts dynamic information from temporal gene embeddings using two complementary signals: an optimal transport residual, which captures gene-specific deviations from global embedding movement, and a KL divergence, which detects changes in local co-expression neighborhoods. Temporal gene-embedding similarity identifies static transcriptional programs, whereas vectorial GSET signals represent coordinated temporal changes among genes, complementing this static structure. Lagged comparisons of these signals further prioritize temporal relationships between programs and candidate bridge genes associated with their transitions. Integrated with CardamomOT, GSET combines static program cores with dynamically retrieved bridge genes into compact, program-informed gene sets for mechanistic GRN inference. In synthetic benchmarks, at equal gene budget these sets recover more of the regulatory links between programs than static selections of the same size, and inference on the edges within the set is comparable to that of the full-gene model on the same gene pairs. On a time course of mouse fibroblasts reprogrammed into induced pluripotent stem cells, GSET traces the transition from the fibroblast program to the cell-cycle program. By providing a dynamic retrieval layer upstream of GRN inference, GSET nominates bridge genes as candidate regulators of cell-state transitions, which, once refined by a mechanistic model such as CardamomOT and confirmed by perturbation experiments, could open the way to controlling these transitions.

preprints.title: Human lymphatic organoids reconstruct convergent developmental routes to functional lymphatic vessels
preprints.abstract: The lymphatic vasculature maintains fluid balance, regulates immune surveillance, and supports tissue repair, yet how human lymphatic vessels arise and acquire specialized functions remains poorly understood. Here, guided by single-cell and spatial analyses of human embryos, we found that both lateral plate and paraxial mesoderm converge on venous endothelial intermediates with cardinal vein-like characteristics prior to lymphatic specification. Informed by these developmental trajectories, we generated three-dimensional lymphatic organoids from human pluripotent stem cells through two distinct mesodermal routes. The organoids formed capillary-like vascular networks with emerging button-like junctions and distinct endothelial and stromal programs. The lymphatic organoids were transcriptionally benchmarked to human fetal lymphatic endothelium. The organoids supported immune-cell interactions and antigen accumulation and, following transplantation, exhibited interstitial tracer uptake and transport. These findings establish a platform for investigating how distinct developmental origins shape human lymphatic specification, vascular organization, and function, with applications to lymphatic disease modeling and tissue repair.

preprints.title: Machine learning guided design of strong transcriptional activation domains
preprints.abstract: Artificial intelligence has accelerated the design of structured proteins, but it remains difficult to design functional intrinsically disordered proteins because of weak structural constraints and poorly defined sequence-to-function relationships1. Activation domains (ADs), transcription factor regions that recruit coactivators, are an excellent test case for the de novo design of intrinsically disordered sequences. ADs are one of the oldest groups of functional intrinsically disordered sequences2 and designed ADs have applications in synthetic biology, biotechnology, and agriculture. We computationally generated 500,000 candidate sequences that resembled known ADs and predicted AD function with extant machine learning models, including three neural networks. From high-scoring sequences, we selected 18,750 for experimental validation in yeast. Surprisingly, >90% of the 16,770 well-measured sequences function as ADs. Sequences predicted to be active by multiple models were stronger, motivating development of a fast and accurate consensus AD predictor, MADRIGAL. A number of our designed ADs retain functionality across fungi, plants, and human cells. This work illustrates a generalizable paradigm for incorporating sequence-to-function models into the design loop to efficiently generate functional intrinsically disordered sequences.

preprints.title: Systemic Analysis of Patient Derived Esophageal Epithelial Organoid Model Reveals Cell State Heterogeneity and Conservation of Differentiation Hierarchy
preprints.abstract: Background and Aims: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) features prominent epithelial dysregulation that persists despite resolution of eosinophilia. Interleukin-13 (IL-13) is known to be a key upstream driver of epithelial abnormalities in EoE. We sought to benchmark an IL-13 esophageal organoid model against the in vivo epithelial state in EoE at a single cell resolution, to define in the role of IL-13 in aberrant epithelial development and inflammation in EoE, and to validate the IL-13 organoid as a model system to study the epithelial changes seen in EoE. Methods: We performed scRNA-Seq on esophageal biopsies from control and EoE patients, and esophageal biopsy-derived organoids with or without IL-13. We compared cellular composition, differentiation trajectories, pathway enrichment, and differential gene expression within both systems, and assessed findings at a protein level. Results: Seven distinct epithelial cell clusters were identified and preserved in both biopsies and organoids. EoE biopsies demonstrated expansion of cycling cells, whereas IL-13-treated organoids showed shift in the composition of the suprabasal compartments. Pseudotime topology was preserved across tissues, with a shift away from terminal differentiation in both EoE biopsies and IL-13-treated organoids. IL-13 reproduced changes in the transcription of central EoE genes and the dysregulation of epithelial proliferation and differentiation pathways seen in EoE. There was broad activation of immune related pathways within both EoE biopsies and IL-13-treated organoids, however, biopsies additionally showed activation in several immune and extracellular matrix remodeling programs that IL-13 alone did not reproduce. Conclusion: IL-13-treated esophageal organoids replicate key epithelial features of EoE including dysregulated epithelial development, impaired cornification, and inflammatory signals, while preserving lineage architecture, providing a tractable platform for epithelial-targeted mechanistic and therapeutic studies.

last_author.name: Ruffner, M. A.
last_author.affiliation: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia

preprints.title: Uncovering cross-signal interactions in single-cell and spatial omics
preprints.abstract: Individual cells simultaneously encode multiple biological signals in their gene expression profiles, including spatial position, circadian phase, and disease state. These signals can be entangled in complex ways, including circadian patterns that vary along disease progression and cell cycle dynamics that shift along developmental trajectories. While methods to disentangle such signals have been recently developed, characterizing the interaction itself between multicellular signals along with its effects on tissue function, localizing cellular subpopulations which exhibit signal interactions, and identifying potential candidate genes which drive such interactions, all remain major challenges. We present CRISP which characterizes signal interactions in single-cell gene expression data based on the correspondence between the multiple, probabilistic signal-specific projections of the data. Across simulations with tunable couplings and four single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets, CRISP recovers diverse biological signal interactions and localizes them to informative cellular subpopulations and groups of associated genes; CRISP distinguishes healthy from fibrotic liver samples and localizes the loss of zonation-position coupling to individual fibrotic hepatocytes, resolves the asymmetric coupling of TGF-{beta} response, EMT, and cell-cycle phase to specific cell subpopulations, and flags transcriptionally delayed hepatocytes in Plasmodium liver infection. Beyond quantifying and localizing signal interactions, CRISP can refine existing labels, uncover continuous cellular transitions and reveal condition-associated genes.

preprints.title: A compact motif vocabulary is differentially interpreted across human cell types
preprints.abstract: How a common genome generates diverse human cell types may depend less on distinct cis-regulatory vocabularies than on context-dependent use of a shared one. We have developed CNN-CR, an interpretable neural network that learns regulatory motifs while predicting gene expression across 116 human biosamples. Promoter regulation proves highly compressible: dozens of recurrent motif families retain most of the predictive information of much larger cell-type-specific vocabularies and generalize to cellular contexts excluded from their discovery. These motifs are conserved at their binding sites and enriched at fine-mapped regulatory variants. Cellular context acts at two levels: chromatin state gates which motif instances are available for regulatory use, whereas reader identity determines how accessible motifs are interpreted. ChIP-seq data reveal frequent shifts in reader occupancy across cell types, and genome-scale perturbations support corresponding context-dependent reader functions. Thus, regulatory diversity can emerge through differential access to and interpretation of a compact shared DNA vocabulary.

last_author.name: Wang, W.
last_author.affiliation: University of California, San Diego

preprints.title: A comparative transcriptomic framework across kidney organoid, assembloid, and transplantation models
preprints.abstract: Human kidney organoids recapitulate key aspects of renal development and have emerged as valuable platforms for disease modeling, nephrotoxicity screening, and therapeutic development. The field now includes a wide range of emerging protocols with distinct cellular compositions and maturation states, which complicates systematic comparison and model selection. Here, we integrated single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomes from 11 studies spanning kidney organoid and assembloids, both in vitro and following transplantation, benchmarked against fetal and adult kidney references. Transcriptional maturation toward adult identity is compartment specific and does not correlate with protocol complexity. Assembloid protocols show the most adult-like podocyte and distal nephron signatures, transplantation is associated with enhanced tubular oxidative metabolic features, only protocols incorporating ureteric progenitors reliably generate collecting-duct lineages, and no protocol achieves mature adult proximal tubule identity. Annotating against either fetal or adult kidney reference alone leads to misassignment, because early fetal nephron epithelium transcriptionally resembles injury-dedifferentiated adult proximal tubule cells. Assembloid and transplantation models share elevated mechanosensing pathway expression independently of vascularization. Together, these findings provide a framework for kidney organoid model selection.

last_author.name: Ortega, M. A.

preprints.title: A comprehensive map of the sequence basis of transcription initiation in humans
preprints.abstract: Transcription initiation is a key marker of active enhancers and promoters. Here we describe an atlas of efficient and interpretable deep learning models trained on over 200 transcription initiation profiling experiments representing all major human organs and many cancer types. We show that our models accurately predict initiation patterns from local DNA sequence and decode their sequence determinants across diverse cellular contexts.

last_author.name: Kundaje, A.
last_author.affiliation: Stanford University

preprints.title: A conserved pituitary response to tissue loss controls regeneration across vertebrates
preprints.abstract: Regenerating complex tissues requires coordination between local cellular responses and body-wide systemic signals. As a central endocrine regulator, the pituitary is well positioned to coordinate this process. Here, we identify the pituitary as an injury-responsive regulator of axolotl limb and tilapia fin regeneration. Limb loss triggered sustained transcriptional responses in the axolotl pituitary. Single-cell transcriptomics linked pituitary loss to altered gene expression in prolactin- and growth hormone-responsive limb cells. Local disruption of the prolactin receptor impaired digit formation, whereas combined hormone treatment partially restored regeneration in hypophysectomized axolotls. In tilapia, pituitary removal impaired fin regeneration and prolactin-related signaling. Mouse digits differed from axolotls and tilapia in how and when they received pituitary signals during regeneration, suggesting pituitary-dependent regrowth is evolutionarily divergent among highly regenerative vertebrates.

last_author.name: Whited, J. L.
last_author.affiliation: Harvard University

preprints.title: A spin glass representation of hierarchical gene regulation and the partial resolution of frustration
preprints.abstract: Gene regulatory networks are directed and often contain loops. A loop can place competing demands on its genes, so that no expression state satisfies every regulatory interaction. In statistical physics such a conflict is called frustration. Existing spin-glass models of tissues assume symmetric regulation, and studies of frustration consider single cells. We develop a nonreciprocal multicellular Ising model that couples a directed regulatory network in each cell to random, symmetric signalling between neighbouring cells. We define intracellular and intercellular frustration densities, which count the unsatisfied interactions within a cell and with its neighbours. We study six exemplar nine-gene networks that share a downstream cascade and differ in an upstream three-gene motif. In isolated cells the motif sets the frustration. Negative feedback loops pass frustration around the loop, and their genes keep switching. The incoherent feedforward loop holds frustration at a single gene and freezes. When cells communicate, they form spatial clusters with shared expression profiles, and conflict between neighbours concentrates at cluster boundaries. Stronger coupling lowers intercellular frustration and raises intracellular frustration. Frustration is therefore resolved only in part: cells satisfy more of the couplings to their neighbours by satisfying fewer of their own regulatory interactions. Varying the coupling strength reveals a transition near the value at which the combined input of a cell's eight neighbours matches a single regulatory interaction. Below it, cells follow their own networks and the tissue fragments. Our framework links the structure of gene regulatory networks to the stability of gene expression in cells and tissues.

last_author.name: Stumpf, M. P. H.
